## ac642cf1-e1c8-4490-9caa-814476453870
The official Figma MCP server. Use this server whenever the user wants to create, generate, edit, implement, or sync any design, UI, screen, component, mockup, or visual — in Figma, FigJam, Figma Make, or Figma Slides — and whenever the user mentions Figma or provides a figma.com URL.

This server bridges code and design in both directions, and supports designing from scratch using existing design systems and codebases.

CAPABILITIES:
- Read designs FROM Figma into code (get_design_context, get_screenshot, get_metadata, get_figjam)
- Write designs INTO Figma from code, intent, or existing components (use_figma, generate_figma_design, create_new_file, upload_assets)
- Bridge code and design via Code Connect (get_code_connect_map, add_code_connect_map)
- Create diagrams and FigJam content (generate_diagram, get_figjam)

WHEN TO USE THESE TOOLS:
- The user wants to create, mock up, or generate any UI, screen, component, or design — even if Figma isn't named
- The user wants to implement a design as code (design-to-code)
- The user wants to push a page, view, or component into Figma (code-to-design)
- The user wants to update, sync, or edit an existing Figma file
- The user shares a figma.com URL
- The user wants to build or extend a design system, design tokens, or component library
- The user wants to create a diagram in FigJam

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

- playwright-skill: Complete browser automation with Playwright. Auto-detects dev servers, writes clean test scripts to /tmp. Test pages, fill forms, take screenshots, check responsive design, validate UX, test login flows, check links, automate any browser task. Use when user wants to test websites, automate browser interactions, validate web functionality, or perform any browser-based testing.
- audit-tier: Identify the protection tier, owner, and import blast radius of a file or directory under overrides/. Use before editing anything you're unsure about.
- code-quality: Audit recently changed or specified files for code quality issues — naming, circular imports, TypeScript coverage, test/story existence, and structural debt. Read-only. Use after implementing a feature or before opening a PR.
- code-review: AI-powered code review using CodeRabbit. Default code-review skill. Trigger for any explicit review request AND autonomously when the agent thinks a review is needed (code/PR/quality/security).
- contentful-register-component: Register a Zimmermann React component with Contentful Studio Experiences. Use when a developer asks to register, add, or expose a React component to Contentful, or when they need to create a Contentful component definition for an existing component.
- feature-spec: Turn a plain-English feature request into a scoped implementation plan before any code is written. Asks one clarifying question at a time, then produces a spec Claude Code can execute safely. Use this before starting any non-trivial implementation session.
- generate-changelog: Generate a release changelog from conventional commits and upstream baseline notes. Produces audience-specific outputs for the dev team, QA, product, and GitHub Release. Use before cutting a release branch or when preparing release notes.
- new-component: Scaffold a new Zimmermann component under overrides/app/components/ — TypeScript, Chakra-first, with a paired Storybook story. Use whenever a new custom component is needed.
- onboarding: Interactive onboarding for new developers and QA engineers joining the Zimmermann PWA Kit project. Asks role at the start, checks the mechanical setup items, then orients the person to the rules and tools relevant to their role and squad. Run this in the first Claude Code session on a new machine or a first day on the project.
- pr-checklist: Generate a PR description and merge checklist based on the files changed on the current branch. Pairs with /code-quality.
- project-init: One-time project setup walkthrough. Runs the state detection script, fixes automatable items, asks one question at a time for human-input items, and updates the 7.1c CI/CD & Environment Setup Checklist Confluence page as each item is confirmed. Run this once when setting up the project for the first time, or when returning to check setup status.
- qa-generate: Generate a Gherkin .feature file and Playwright test spec from a Jira story. Human-in-the-lead — Lead QA validates the .feature before Playwright is generated. Use for any new storefront user journey that needs E2E test coverage.
- scope-check: Review a proposed Claude Code prompt for scope safety before it runs. Classifies every likely-touched file by tier and verdicts the prompt SAFE / RISKY / BLOCKED, rewriting it when needed.
- session-start: Run the mandatory session start ritual — reads tracking docs, runs branch + health checks, states current position. Use at the start of every coding session.
- upstream-sync-review: Review the release notes / changelog for a new @salesforce/retail-react-app version before bumping. Lightweight policy — see .docs/upstreamPolicy.md.

- commit-commands:commit: Create a git commit

- plugin-dev:create-plugin: Guided end-to-end plugin creation workflow with component design, implementation, and validation

- figma:figma-create-new-file: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE every `create_new_file` tool call. NEVER call `create_new_file` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user wants a new blank Figma file — a new design, FigJam, or Slides file — or when you need a fresh file before calling `use_figma`. Usage — /figma-create-new-file [editorType] [fileName] (e.g. /figma-create-new-file figjam My Whiteboard, /figma-create-new-file slides Q3 Review)
- figma:figma-design-to-code: **MANDATORY prerequisite** — you MUST invoke this skill BEFORE calling the `get_design_context` Figma MCP tool. You MUST trigger this skill whenever the user wants to implement, build, port, or code up a Figma design as code. Example prompts (not exhaustive) are 'implement this Figma design', 'build this screen from Figma', 'turn this Figma into code', 'design to code'. This skill provides critical instructions and steps to the agent on how to correctly implement Figma designs in code and must NOT be skipped.
- figma:figma-generate-design: Use this skill alongside figma-use when the task involves translating an application page, view, or multi-section layout into Figma. Triggers: 'write to Figma', 'create in Figma from code', 'push page to Figma', 'take this app/page and build it in Figma', 'create a screen', 'build a landing page in Figma', 'update the Figma screen to match code', 'convert this modal/dialog/drawer/panel to Figma'. This is the preferred workflow skill whenever the user wants to build or update a full page, modal, dialog, drawer, sidebar, panel, or any composed multi-section view in Figma from code or a description. Discovers design system components, variables, and styles from Code Connect files, existing screens, and library search, then imports them and assembles views incrementally section-by-section using design system tokens instead of hardcoded values.
- figma:figma-generate-diagram: MANDATORY prerequisite — load this skill BEFORE every `generate_diagram` tool call. NEVER call `generate_diagram` directly without loading this skill first. Trigger whenever the user asks to create, generate, draw, render, sketch, or build a diagram — flowchart, architecture diagram, sequence diagram, ERD or entity-relationship diagram, state diagram or state machine, gantt chart, or timeline. Also trigger when the user mentions Mermaid syntax or wants a system architecture, decision tree, dependency graph, API call flow, auth handshake, schema, or pipeline visualized in FigJam. Routes to type-specific guidance, sets universal Mermaid constraints, and tells you when to use a different diagram type or skip the tool entirely (mindmaps, pie charts, class diagrams, etc.).
- figma:figma-generate-library: Build or update a professional-grade design system in Figma from a codebase. Also use when the user asks to create or generate any component in Figma — even a single one — since components require proper variable foundations, variant states, and design token bindings to be production-quality. This skill teaches WHAT to build and in WHAT ORDER — it complements the `figma-use` skill which teaches HOW to call the Plugin API. Both skills should be loaded together.
- figma:figma-implement-motion: Translates Figma motion and animations into production-ready application code. Use whenever the user mentions Swift, SwiftUI, iOS, iPhone, or iPad — in EITHER direction — translating a Figma design into SwiftUI (design → code), or pushing SwiftUI views / screens / tokens back into a Figma file (code → design). Triggers on phrases like 'implement this Figma design in SwiftUI', 'build this screen in Swift', 'push this SwiftUI view to Figma', 'mirror my Swift code in a Figma file', or whenever a Figma URL appears alongside `.swift` files / an `.xcodeproj`. message.content:
for this PR review, here's how we'll run it:



PR REVIEW AS A CLOSED LOOP



The shape is four stages. What makes it work is that you hold the ground truth and the adjudication, and delegate only the reading. Reviewers are cheap and fallible; measurements are expensive and authoritative. Keep those on opposite sides of the line.





STAGE 0 — ESTABLISH GROUND TRUTH YOURSELF



Before spinning up a single agent, do four things. Every later stage depends on this.



Check out the PR branch and record the frame: base SHA, head SHA, files changed, plus/minus lines. You will refer back to this constantly when a reviewer claims something changed that did not.



Get the ticket verbatim. Not your summary, not the PR description's paraphrase — the actual acceptance criteria as written. Every scope argument later gets decided against those words, and handing reviewers your compression of it pre-decides the scope question for them. A reviewer given a wrong premise wastes an entire pass.



Run every deterministic gate and write down the raw numbers. Typecheck, tests, lint, build, any repo-specific audit script. Then run them again on the base SHA. This is the PR-specific step people skip: without a baseline you cannot distinguish a failure the PR introduced from one it inherited, and you will burn reviewer budget on both.



Read the repo's own convention docs — CONTRIBUTING, AGENTS.md, .claude/rules/, whatever exists. These are the rubric. A reviewer applying general best practice instead of house rules generates noise that reads like signal.



Three traps to check before trusting any gate number:



1. Non-zero at a healthy baseline. Lint exits 1 with pre-existing errors; an audit script exits 1 with known violations. Diff the counts, ignore the exit code. Treating non-zero as failure means nothing ever passes.



2. Passes having run nothing. Vitest's passWithNoTests, a path filter matching zero files, a --grep matching no tests. Assert on the reported item count, never the exit code.



3. Stderr noise on a passing run. Parser warnings, deprecation notices. Note them explicitly so reviewers do not flag them as findings.





STAGE 1 — FAN OUT



Launch three or four reviewers in parallel, fresh contexts, not forks. A fork inherits your assumptions about what "done" looks like, which is exactly what you want tested.



Give each: the diff, the ticket verbatim, and your measured gate numbers. Then forbid them from re-running the gates. You already measured; their budget should go entirely on what gates cannot see.



Briefs should be distinct but overlapping — that overlap is the mechanism. Two agents converging independently is your confidence signal; two agents disagreeing is where you learn something.



Angles that work, adapted to what the diff touches:



- Correctness and regression. Does it do what the ticket says? What breaks that the diff does not obviously touch? Trace call sites of anything modified.

- Conventions and structure. Against the repo's own docs. Naming, layering, imports, required tests and stories, ownership and tier rules.

- Contract fidelity. If the PR ports, wraps, overrides or extends something, diff against the original and confirm every delta is deliberate. Prop surfaces, public APIs, error behaviour.

- Failure modes. Error handling, silent failures, fallbacks that mask bugs, security-sensitive paths — logged credentials, unsanitised HTML, injection.



Constraints to impose on every reviewer. These are the parts that produce findings rather than summaries. Phrase them how you like, but keep all of them:



- Falsify, do not confirm. Try to break each claim the PR makes about itself.

- Cite file:line, and label every finding CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE — reproduced versus reasoned-but-unproven. That distinction is what lets you triage fast later.

- Severity: BLOCKER, DEFECT, or NOTE.

- When a count moves, prove which items moved, not just how many. A total going 19 to 14 looks like proof and is not — it is equally consistent with a deleted item or a mutated value. Where the set is small enough, settle identity by enumerating it.

- For any check whose pass you are relying on, try to make it pass wrongly. Inject a decoy that should fail and confirm it does. A check never made to fail has not been shown capable of failing.

- Any "X exists nowhere" claim must state its search scope in the same sentence. Scope is part of the finding, not context around it.

- Separate what the author changed from what was already there. Pre-existing issues are NOTEs unless the PR's own premise makes them defects.

- Mandatory closing section: "What I could not verify." Name what you could not reach and why. If you think the space is covered, show the search. An empty section with no reasoning is a failed brief.





STAGE 2 — ADJUDICATE, AND THIS IS YOURS ALONE



This is where the loop earns its cost. Do not delegate it.



Where reviewers agree, accept it. Independent convergence is the strongest signal you have.



Where they disagree, go to source yourself. Do not average them, and do not take the more confident one — confidence and correctness are not correlated in agent output. Record which you checked and what settled it.



Where a reviewer's conclusion is broader than its search supports, downgrade it. This is the single most common failure mode: the search is correct, the claim overreaches. "This exists nowhere" almost always means "nowhere I looked."



Expect roughly a third of findings to be confidently wrong. A reviewer refuting its own sub-finding is the system working, not budget wasted.



Treat inherited attributions as claims, not measurements. If a reviewer tells you "this line is unchanged from upstream," that is a claim it may have inherited from the PR's own comments. Verify before repeating it — passing one through as fact is an easy way to launder an error into your own report.



Scope in both directions. Flag under-delivery and over-delivery against the ticket. Anything beyond what was asked gets surfaced for a human ruling — do not silently accept it, and do not demand its removal either.



And name one premise everyone agreed on, then make someone attack it. Shared assumptions are invisible precisely because they are shared. This is the highest-yield single move in the whole workflow.





STAGE 3 — WHAT YOU PRODUCE



Four sections:



1. Gate table. Every number you measured, against baseline.

2. Findings, ranked, BLOCKERs first. Each one: file:line, a one-sentence statement of the defect, a concrete failure scenario (inputs to wrong output), and the fix.

3. What nobody verified. The union of the reviewers' gaps, minus anything you closed. State plainly what a human still has to check by hand or in a browser. This section is the honest one, and it is what stops a clean result reading as proof.

4. Your adjudications. Every disagreement and what settled it.



Nothing gets posted to the PR unless you decide to post it.





IF YOU TRIM IT, KEEP THESE FOUR



Everything above is scaffolding around four instructions that do most of the work:



Mandatory "what I could not verify." Reviewers naturally report what they checked, which reads as completeness. Forcing an explicit gap list surfaces the thing nobody looked at.



Prove which items moved, not how many. Each level of rigour — moved number, then conserved total, then identity by exhaustion — closes a hole the previous one leaves open.



State your search scope in the same sentence. Turns an overreaching conclusion back into an accurate one.



Do not ratify the chain. Make the shared premise explicit and attack it.

### qa.yml — `detect-changes`

No `if:`. Always runs. Produces four outputs used downstream: `e2e`, `vitest`, `storybook`, `e2e_scope`, `jira_keys`. Also uploads artifact `e2e-scope.json` consumed by `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`.

Scope logic (qa.yml lines 148–171):
- If base ref is `release/*` → `e2e_scope=full`
- If no e2e-relevant files changed → `e2e_scope=skip`
- If every e2e-relevant changed file is also in the `e2e_homepage` allow-list → `e2e_scope=homepage`

### qa.yml — `unit-tests`

`if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.vitest == 'true'` (qa.yml line 246)

Skips when no file in `overrides/**`, `vitest.config.*`, `vitest.setup.ts`, `tsconfig.json`, `babel.config.js` changed since the last remote commit AND runtime deps (the `dependencies` block of `package.json`) did not change.

### qa.yml — `storybook-test`

`if: needs.detect-changes.outputs.storybook == 'true'` (qa.yml line 389)

Skips when no file in `overrides/app/components/**`, `overrides/app/pages/**`, `overrides/app/hooks/**`, `overrides/app/theme/**`, `overrides/app/types/**`, `.storybook/**`, `package.json`, `package-lock.json` changed since the last remote commit.

```yaml

  needs.detect-changes.outputs.e2e == 'true' &&
  needs.detect-changes.outputs.e2e_scope != 'skip' &&
  (needs.unit-tests.result == 'success' || needs.unit-tests.result == 'skipped')
```
(qa.yml lines 462–466)

Skip paths:
1. Workflow cancelled.
2. No e2e-relevant path changed.
3. `e2e_scope == 'skip'` (diff touches paths outside every area's allow-list on a develop-PR).
4. `unit-tests` failed (not `success` and not `skipped`).

If the `--grep` matches no collected spec (e.g. all homepage specs are excluded by `testIgnore` on a project), Playwright exits 0 with zero tests. No explicit guard against a zero-match run exists.

### qa.yml — `e2e-browserstack` (release/\*\* only)

```yaml

  always() &&
  needs.detect-changes.outputs.e2e == 'true' &&
  (needs.unit-tests.result == 'success' || needs.unit-tests.result == 'skipped') &&
  contains(github.base_ref, 'release/')
```
(qa.yml lines 605–609)

Skip paths: base ref does not contain `release/`; e2e not relevant; `unit-tests` failed. Note: `always()` means this runs even if `unit-tests` was skipped, but the explicit result check provides the actual gate.

The build name here is hardcoded to `github.run_number` (qa.yml line 629) — `computeBuildName.mjs` is not called from this job. `SPRINT_NUMBER` env var is set to the run number, which feeds `browserstack.yml`'s `buildName: "Sprint-${SPRINT_NUMBER}"`.

### deploy-preview.yml — `deploy-preview`

No `if:`. Runs on every matching push (branch filter is in `on:`). `cancel-in-progress: false` on the concurrency group.

### e2e-browserstack-preview.yml — `e2e-browserstack`

Job-level: `if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion != 'cancelled'`

Then a chain of per-step conditions:

1. "Find open PR for this branch" (always runs): sets `skip=true` → no further steps if no open PR found, or if the PR's base is not `develop`.
2. "Detect Jira story keys": only runs if `steps.pr.outputs.skip == 'false'`. If keys are empty, all downstream BrowserStack steps are skipped.
3. "Look up matching QA run": only runs if `steps.jira.outputs.keys != ''`.
4. "Download e2e-relevance artifact": only runs if `steps.qa-run.outputs.run_id != ''`; `continue-on-error: true`.
5. "Check e2e relevance": only runs if `steps.jira.outputs.keys != ''`. Sets `relevant=false` if the downloaded artifact says `e2e: "false"`. Fail-open: if the artifact could not be downloaded or read, defaults to `relevant=true`.
6. All remaining steps (build name, BrowserStack run) only execute if `steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'`.

Zero-test / zero-execution paths:
- Deploy Preview was cancelled → job skips entirely.
- No open PR for the pushed branch.
- PR base ref is not `develop`.
- No `SFCC-NNN` key anywhere in PR title, body, or branch name.
- `e2e-scope.json` downloaded from the QA run says `e2e: "false"`.
- `--grep` built from Jira keys (e.g. `@SFCC-751`) matches no collected spec.

### zephyr-results-sync.yml — `sync`

`if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion != 'cancelled'` (zephyr-results-sync.yml line ~42)

Zero-sync path (exits 0): If no BrowserStack build named `Sprint-{name}` exists in the project, the script logs "No BrowserStack build found — nothing to sync" and returns normally (script line ~259–262). This is the expected path for most QA runs where `e2e-browserstack` was skipped.

## 4. `zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs` — Inputs, Outputs, HTTP Calls, Error Behaviour

**File**: `scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs` (359 lines)

**Inputs**: Nine required env vars checked at startup (lines ~60–63); if any is absent, `die()` is called immediately. Also reads `GITHUB_SERVER_URL`, `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, `GITHUB_RUN_ID`, `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (all auto-provided by Actions).

**Outputs**: Writes a Markdown summary table to `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. Exits 0 on success or normal no-op; exits non-zero on fatal errors.

**External HTTP calls** (all via a `fetchJson` wrapper that throws on non-2xx):

1. `GET https://api-automation.browserstack.com/ext/v1/projects` — paginated; finds BrowserStack project by name.
2. `GET https://api-automation.browserstack.com/ext/v1/projects/{id}/builds?unique_build_names={buildName}` — finds the build for this run.
3. `GET https://api-automation.browserstack.com/ext/v1/builds/{buildId}/testRuns` — paginated; walks `hierarchy[].children[].details` to extract per-test name, tags, status, session URL, and failure logs.
4. `POST {ZEPHYR_TESTEXECUTIONS_URL}` — one call per test carrying a `@zephyr:` tag; creates a Zephyr Scale execution record.
5. `GET {JIRA_URL}/rest/api/3/issue/{storyKey}?fields=assignee` — reads assignee of the related story (for defect auto-assignment).
6. `GET {JIRA_URL}/rest/api/3/user/search?query={email}` — resolves a git committer email to a Jira account ID (fallback when story has no assignee).
7. `POST {JIRA_URL}/rest/api/3/issue` — files a Bug issue on every failed test that also has an `@SFCC-NNN` story tag.

**BrowserStack tag stripping**: The API returns tags without the leading `@` (e.g. `zephyr:SFCC-T285`, not `@zephyr:SFCC-T285`). The `zephyrKeyTag` and `storyKeyTag` functions account for this (script lines ~153–160).

**Error/exit behaviour**:
- `die(msg)` → `process.exit(1)`: on missing required env var; BrowserStack project not found; any unhandled rejection in `main()`.
- `warn(msg)` → `console.error('::warning::...')`, execution continues: per-test Zephyr POST failure; Jira assignee lookup failure; git blame fallback failure; Jira account-ID resolution failure; Jira defect creation failure. A failure on one test does not stop processing of subsequent tests.
- Normal exit 0: no build found for this run (expected for most QA runs where BrowserStack didn't execute); build found but zero tests carry a `@zephyr:` tag; all tests processed successfully.

**Not yet live-verified** (explicitly noted in the script's doc comment, line ~46): the `hierarchy[]` response shape from the BrowserStack Get Tests API has never been exercised against a real build payload in this account.

Job-level: `if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion != 'cancelled'`

1. "Find open PR for this branch" (always runs): sets `skip=true` → no further steps if no open PR found, or if the PR's base is not `develop`.
2. "Detect Jira story keys": only runs if `steps.pr.outputs.skip == 'false'`. If keys are empty, all downstream BrowserStack steps are skipped.
3. "Look up matching QA run": only runs if `steps.jira.outputs.keys != ''`.
4. "Download e2e-relevance artifact": only runs if `steps.qa-run.outputs.run_id != ''`; `continue-on-error: true`.
5. "Check e2e relevance": only runs if `steps.jira.outputs.keys != ''`. Sets `relevant=false` if the downloaded artifact says `e2e: "false"`. Fail-open: if the artifact could not be downloaded or read, defaults to `relevant=true`.
6. All remaining steps (build name, BrowserStack run) only execute if `steps.relevance.outputs.relevant == 'true'`.

Zero-test / zero-execution paths:
- Deploy Preview was cancelled → job skips entirely.
- No open PR for the pushed branch.
- PR base ref is not `develop`.
- No `SFCC-NNN` key anywhere in PR title, body, or branch name.
- `e2e-scope.json` downloaded from the QA run says `e2e: "false"`.
- `--grep` built from Jira keys (e.g. `@SFCC-751`) matches no collected spec.

`if: github.event.workflow_run.conclusion != 'cancelled'` (zephyr-results-sync.yml line ~42)

## 4. `zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs` — Inputs, Outputs, HTTP Calls, Error Behaviour

**File**: `scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs` (359 lines)

**Inputs**: Nine required env vars checked at startup (lines ~60–63); if any is absent, `die()` is called immediately. Also reads `GITHUB_SERVER_URL`, `GITHUB_REPOSITORY`, `GITHUB_RUN_ID`, `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` (all auto-provided by Actions).

**Outputs**: Writes a Markdown summary table to `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`. Exits 0 on success or normal no-op; exits non-zero on fatal errors.

**External HTTP calls** (all via a `fetchJson` wrapper that throws on non-2xx):

1. `GET https://api-automation.browserstack.com/ext/v1/projects` — paginated; finds BrowserStack project by name.
2. `GET https://api-automation.browserstack.com/ext/v1/projects/{id}/builds?unique_build_names={buildName}` — finds the build for this run.
3. `GET https://api-automation.browserstack.com/ext/v1/builds/{buildId}/testRuns` — paginated; walks `hierarchy[].children[].details` to extract per-test name, tags, status, session URL, and failure logs.
4. `POST {ZEPHYR_TESTEXECUTIONS_URL}` — one call per test carrying a `@zephyr:` tag; creates a Zephyr Scale execution record.
5. `GET {JIRA_URL}/rest/api/3/issue/{storyKey}?fields=assignee` — reads assignee of the related story (for defect auto-assignment).
6. `GET {JIRA_URL}/rest/api/3/user/search?query={email}` — resolves a git committer email to a Jira account ID (fallback when story has no assignee).
7. `POST {JIRA_URL}/rest/api/3/issue` — files a Bug issue on every failed test that also has an `@SFCC-NNN` story tag.

**BrowserStack tag stripping**: The API returns tags without the leading `@` (e.g. `zephyr:SFCC-T285`, not `@zephyr:SFCC-T285`). The `zephyrKeyTag` and `storyKeyTag` functions account for this (script lines ~153–160).

**Error/exit behaviour**:
- `die(msg)` → `process.exit(1)`: on missing required env var; BrowserStack project not found; any unhandled rejection in `main()`.
- `warn(msg)` → `console.error('::warning::...')`, execution continues: per-test Zephyr POST failure; Jira assignee lookup failure; git blame fallback failure; Jira account-ID resolution failure; Jira defect creation failure. A failure on one test does not stop processing of subsequent tests.
- Normal exit 0: no build found for this run (expected for most QA runs where BrowserStack didn't execute); build found but zero tests carry a `@zephyr:` tag; all tests processed successfully.

**Not yet live-verified** (explicitly noted in the script's doc comment, line ~46): the `hierarchy[]` response shape from the BrowserStack Get Tests API has never been exercised against a real build payload in this account.

Description

Overview
Implement the end-to-end QA pipeline that closes the loop between Zephyr Scale test cases and BrowserStack Automate execution results. This story covers three discrete deliverables that must be in place for the AI-assisted QA methodology to function as designed.

Background
Zephyr test case SFCC-T150 has been created and linked to SFCC-420. The pipeline requires:

A Playwright spec tagged with the Zephyr test case key so BrowserStack knows what it is executing

A GitHub Actions workflow that fetches BrowserStack results and posts execution records back to Zephyr Scale via the EU regional API

A validated end-to-end run confirming the full chain works

Deliverables
Deliverable 1 — Playwright spec (SFCC-T150)

Generate e2e/tests/zimm/integrations/SFCC-420-global-e-job-site-assignments.p1.spec.ts

Spec must be tagged with Zephyr test case key SFCC-T150

Scenarios must cover all 6 BDD scenarios in SFCC-T150

Selectors via POM only — no inline selectors

Tagged @SFCC-420 @global-e @integration @p1

Deliverable 2 — GitHub Actions sync script

New workflow: .github/workflows/zephyr-results-sync.yml

Triggers on completion of BrowserStack Automate run in CI

Fetches BrowserStack session results via BrowserStack REST API

Maps BrowserStack pass/fail to Zephyr test case key via spec tag

Posts execution record to Zephyr Scale EU endpoint: https://de.api.zephyrscale.smartbear.com/v2/testexecutions

Attaches BrowserStack session URL and HAR to Zephyr execution record

Zephyr API token stored as GitHub Actions secret: ZEPHYR_API_TOKEN

BrowserStack credentials stored as: BROWSERSTACK_USERNAME, BROWSERSTACK_ACCESS_KEY

Deliverable 3 — End-to-end validation

Trigger a BrowserStack run against the new spec

Confirm execution record appears in Zephyr under SFCC-T150

Confirm BrowserStack session URL is attached to the Zephyr execution record

Document any manual steps required for ongoing operation

Rollout Scope

None
Acceptance Criteria


Given a merged Playwright spec tagged with a Zephyr test case key, when BrowserStack Automate completes a run in CI, then an execution record is created in Zephyr Scale under the correct test case with pass/fail status and BrowserStack session URL attached

Given the sync script runs, when it calls the Zephyr API, then it uses the EU regional endpoint https://de.api.zephyrscale.smartbear.com/v2 and not the US default

Given a BrowserStack run fails, when the sync script posts to Zephyr, then the execution record status is Failed and the BrowserStack session URL for debugging is included

Given the pipeline runs end-to-end, when reviewed in Zephyr Scale, then SFCC-T150 shows an execution record linked to the BrowserStack run with correct status

Assumptions

None
Design/Technical Notes


Zephyr Scale instance is on EU/DE regional API: https://de.api.zephyrscale.smartbear.com/v2

Do NOT use the US default endpoint https://api.zephyrscale.smartbear.com/v2 — returns unknown token errors

BrowserStack Automate REST API: Overview of Automate API | BrowserStack Docs 

Zephyr Scale test executions API: POST /testexecutions with testCaseKey, testCycleKey, statusName, comment

The .browserstack.yml is already scoped to e2e/tests/zimm — new spec picked up automatically

Playwright spec naming convention: {JIRA-KEY}-{description}.{priority}.spec.ts

# Closed-Loop Review — PR #61 (SFCC-751)

## Context

PR #61 "SFCC-751: BrowserStack/Zephyr Scale QA automation pipeline" is up for our review.
42 files, +2886/−266, 20 commits, `feature/browserstack-ci-automation` → `develop`,
author TimLavelleACC. CodeRabbit has approved after several CHANGES_REQUESTED rounds; no
human review yet (`reviewDecision: REVIEW_REQUIRED`).

We are running it as a four-stage closed loop: I hold ground truth and adjudication,
delegated agents do only the reading. The reason this PR warrants the full loop rather
than a normal read is established below — **this repo's automated gates are effectively
blind to it**, so the usual "CI is green" signal carries almost no information here.

Confirmed operating constraints:
- **No branch checkout.** The working tree has 29 staged/modified SFCC-89 files. All PR
  access is via the already-fetched read-only ref `pr/61` (`git show pr/61:<path>`).
- **No local gates, no worktree** (user's call, made knowing the coverage finding below).
  The gate table is harvested from the PR's existing CI runs instead. Consequence: **no
  base-vs-head baseline comparison exists**, so we cannot mechanically separate introduced
  from inherited failures. This is a forfeited control and goes in the report's gaps section.
- Four Stage 1 reviewers, all on Opus, fresh contexts (not forks).
- **Nothing is posted to the PR.** Report is delivered here only. AGENTS.md Hard Rule 15
  forbids commenting/committing absent an explicit ask in the current prompt.

---

## Stage 0 — Ground truth (COMPLETE)

### Frame

| | |
|---|---|
| Base (merge-base w/ develop) | `8362b3c` |
| Head | `74e2b82` |
| Diff | 42 files, +2886 / −266, 3842 diff lines / 209 KB, verified untruncated |
| Access | 41/42 files readable at head; `.browserstack.yml` deleted, readable at base |

Cross-checked: `gh pr diff` and local `git diff 8362b3c pr/61` report identical
file/line counts, so the two sources agree independently.

### Acceptance criteria

SFCC-751 supplied verbatim by the user (Atlassian MCP was disconnected this session).
Stored for the briefs; three deliverables (spec / sync workflow / end-to-end validation)
and four AC clauses. **Passed to reviewers verbatim, uncompressed and un-annotated** — my
own scope reading is deliberately withheld so their scope findings stay independent.

### Gate table — the finding that reframes the review

PR #61 touches **zero files under `overrides/`**. Nearly every gate in this repo is scoped
there:

| Gate | Scope | PR files covered | CI result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `npm run lint` | `overrides/**/*.{ts,tsx}` | **0 / 42** | not run in qa.yml |
| `npm run audit:tokens` | `overrides/app/{components,theme/components}/**` | **0 / 42** | not wired to CI; exits 1 at baseline (14 known pre-existing) |
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | tsconfig `include: ['overrides/**/*','vitest.config.ts','vitest.setup.ts']` | **1 / 42** | not run in qa.yml |
| Unit tests (Vitest) | `include: ['overrides/**/*.test.ts(x)']`, `passWithNoTests: true` | **0 / 42** | pass, 1m46s |
| Storybook a11y/interaction | `overrides/**/*.stories.*` | **0 / 42** | pass, 2m57s |
| Playwright E2E (localhost) | — | — | **skipping** |
| Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack) | — | — | **skipping** |
| Deploy Preview | — | — | pass, 5m2s |
| File Tier & Squad Boundary | — | — | pass |

The two green test jobs fired only because `detect-changes` watches `vitest.config.*` and
`package.json` — both changed. They ran the pre-existing `overrides/` suites, which this PR
does not touch. That is worth exactly one thing: evidence the `vitest.config.ts` edit did
not break collection for the existing suite. It is not evidence about any of the 42 files.

**Net: the automated gates verify approximately one file in forty-two, and the PR that
introduces an E2E pipeline has never executed a single E2E test.**

### Why both E2E jobs skipped (mechanism, not guess)

- `e2e-localhost`: `detect-changes` sets `e2e_scope=homepage` only if *every* e2e-relevant
  changed file sits inside the `e2e_homepage` allow-list. This PR also changes `qa.yml`,
  `.github/workflows/**` and more, so it falls to `e2e_scope=skip`, and the job's `if:`
  excludes `skip`.
- `e2e-browserstack` (qa.yml): gated on `contains(github.base_ref, 'release/')`. This PR
  targets `develop`, so it cannot run.
- Per `qa.yml`'s own header comment and prior project notes, **a skipped required check
  reads as passing** on the merge button.

### Trap audit (all three of the named traps are live here)

1. **Non-zero at healthy baseline** — `audit:tokens` exits 1 on a clean tree (14 documented
   pre-existing violations); `test:max-file-size` exits 1 (actual `main.js` ~352 kB vs
   180 kB budget, `vendor.js` ~2 MB vs 550 kB). Neither is in CI. Reviewers must not read
   these exit codes as PR failures.
2. **Passes having run nothing** — `passWithNoTests: true` (`vitest.config.ts:12`);
   Playwright `--grep` with no match exits 0 "0 passed"; `test:contracts` is a permanent
   `echo && exit 0` stub; skipped CI jobs count as passing.
3. **Stderr noise** — none measured locally this run (no local gates); reviewers are told
   not to treat CI log warnings as findings.

### Rubric

House rules are read at **base `8362b3c`**, not head — this PR edits two of the rule files
it would be judged against (`.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`, `.claude/rules/testing.md`).
Rule-file changes are reviewed separately, as changes.

Tier map at base: **12 of 42 paths are Tier 1** (`.browserstack.yml`, `vitest.config.ts`,
`package.json`, `CODEOWNERS`, `scripts/hooks/pre-commit`, both edited `.claude/rules/*`,
and all five `.github/workflows/*`). Zero Tier 2. Nine `e2e/**` paths owned by
`@ZimmermannAU/pwa-qa-team` (untiered). 21 with no CODEOWNERS entry.

### Already settled by me (do not re-litigate)

- **`.browserstack.yml` → `browserstack.yml` is handled, not dropped.** At head,
  `frozenFiles.md:114` re-lists the un-dotted path with the rename rationale
  (browserstack-node-sdk requires that exact filename) and `CODEOWNERS:60` routes it to
  tier-1-approvers. My earlier concern is withdrawn. Still open: `protected-file-guard.yml`
  has no `browserstack` entry at base *or* head, so the CI guard stays blind — pre-existing,
  but this PR edits that guard, which is what makes it arguable.

---

## Stage 1 — Fan out (4 reviewers, Opus, parallel, fresh contexts)

Each reviewer receives: the diff, the **verbatim** AC, the gate table above, the trap audit,
the "already settled" list, and the base-commit rubric instruction. Each is **forbidden from
re-running gates** — budget goes entirely to what gates cannot see.

### Constraints imposed on all four (verbatim in every brief)

- Falsify, do not confirm. Attack each claim the PR makes about itself.
- Cite `file:line`. Label every finding **CONFIRMED** (reproduced) or **PLAUSIBLE**
  (reasoned, unproven).
- Severity: **BLOCKER** / **DEFECT** / **NOTE**.
- When a count moves, prove *which items* moved, not how many. Enumerate identity where the
  set is small enough.
- For any check whose pass you rely on, try to make it pass wrongly — inject a decoy that
  should fail and confirm it does. A check never made to fail has not been shown able to fail.
- Any "X exists nowhere" claim must state its search scope **in the same sentence**.
- Separate author-introduced from pre-existing. Pre-existing → NOTE, unless the PR's own
  premise makes it a defect.
- Mandatory closing section **"What I could not verify"** — name what you could not reach
  and why. If you believe the space is covered, show the search. An empty section with no
  reasoning is a failed brief.

### R1 — Correctness & regression (CI control flow)

Does the pipeline do what the AC says? Trace every path through `qa.yml`,
`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`, `deploy-preview.yml`, `zephyr-results-sync.yml`. Enumerate
every route to a green run that executes zero tests. Specific targets: the
`e2e_scope=homepage` allow-list vs. this PR's own file set; the `--grep` zero-match exit-0
path; `computeBuildName.mjs`'s `unknown-{key}` fallback feeding a build-name lookup that
then finds nothing and exits 0; whether `deploy-preview.yml` firing on every `feature/**`
push contends for a shared MRT target.

### R2 — Conventions, tier & ownership

Rubric = base `8362b3c`. Classify all 42 paths. Adjudicate against AGENTS.md Hard Rules —
**#8** (`vitest.config.ts` is explicitly named never-modify and is modified, +18),
**#7** (`@vitest/coverage-v8` added to devDependencies), **#2/#4** (12 Tier 1 paths).
Check `.docs/temp/SFCC-751-*.md` (+418 lines, author's own AI briefs) are intended as
tracked files. Verify the `.claude/rules/*.md` → `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` mirror is
regenerated, not hand-edited, per `scripts/hooks/pre-commit` §3 and `syncCursorRules.mjs`.

### R3 — Contract fidelity

This PR rewrites its own rubric and moves a Tier 1 file. Diff `.claude/rules/testing.md`
(+163/−20) and `frozenFiles.md` at base vs head and confirm **every delta is deliberate and
describes behaviour that actually exists** — a rules doc asserting a guard that isn't wired
is worse than silence. Same treatment for `browserstack.yml` (46 → 144 lines, not scored as
a rename: what did the rewrite change?), `protected-file-guard.yml`, and the AC's stated
contracts — secret **names**, the Zephyr **EU** endpoint, and the spec **naming convention**.

### R4 — Failure modes & security

Error handling, silent failures, fail-open behaviour, secrets. Targets: every `warn()`-and-
continue path in `zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs` (359 lines); its documented-unverified
BrowserStack `hierarchy[]` response shape; the `ZEPHYR_API_URL` `/testcases`→`/testexecutions`
suffix rewrite when the URL doesn't match the expected pattern; `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`
defaulting `relevant=true` when the relevance artifact can't be read (fail-open onto a
paid BrowserStack run); the new `GH_ENV_READ_TOKEN` secret; `.env.sample` changes against the
pre-commit secret guard; and the script's **automatic Jira Bug creation with auto-assignment**
on every failed test — an outward-facing side effect.

---

## Stage 2 — Adjudication (mine alone, not delegated)

- Reviewers agreeing independently → accept.
- Reviewers disagreeing → go to source myself. Do not average, do not defer to the more
  confident. Record what settled it.
- Conclusion broader than its search → downgrade. Expect this to be the most common defect.
- Expect ~⅓ of findings to be confidently wrong. A reviewer refuting its own sub-finding is
  the system working.
- Treat inherited attributions as claims. In particular, several of this PR's own source
  comments narrate prior CodeRabbit rounds and design rationale; a reviewer repeating one is
  quoting the author, not measuring. Verify before promoting to fact.
- Scope in **both** directions — under-delivery and over-delivery — and surface every
  over-delivery for a human ruling rather than accepting or demanding removal.

**Shared premise to attack (the highest-yield move):** everyone in the chain — author,
CodeRabbit's approval, the green check marks — has proceeded as if *this pipeline has been
demonstrated to work*. Nothing in the evidence supports that: zero E2E tests ran on this PR,
the BrowserStack response shape is documented in the script as never exercised against a real
payload, and the build-name and sync paths both degrade silently to no-ops. I will assign one
reviewer to attack that premise directly and will not let convergence on it substitute for
evidence.

**Pre-registered adjudication checkpoints** (things I will verify at source regardless of
what reviewers say, so a miss is visible):
1. Whether the two shipped specs satisfy Deliverable 1 as written, on every axis the AC
   specifies — path, extension, filename convention, Jira tag, Zephyr key, scenario coverage.
2. Whether `SFCC-751_mobile-header-nav-gap.spec.js` is a live unannotated failing assertion
   (`expect(...).toBeGreaterThan(0)` at :42 under a plain `test(` at :26, with a comment
   saying it is expected to fail today) and, if so, what it does to a `release/**` full-suite
   run — where it is in scope for both `e2e-localhost` and `e2e-browserstack`.
3. The Zephyr endpoint region and the `ZEPHYR_API_TOKEN` vs `ZEPHYR_API_KEY` secret name.
4. Deliverable 3 (end-to-end validation) — whether any evidence of it exists anywhere.

---

## Stage 3 — Report (delivered in chat, posted nowhere)

1. **Gate table** — as measured, with coverage-of-diff stated alongside pass/fail, and the
   absent baseline called out explicitly.
2. **Findings**, ranked, BLOCKERs first. Each: `file:line`, one-sentence defect statement,
   a concrete failure scenario (inputs → wrong output), and the fix.
3. **What nobody verified** — union of the four reviewers' gaps minus what I closed, plus
   the forfeited baseline comparison and anything needing a human in a browser or a live
   BrowserStack/Zephyr/Jira account.
4. **My adjudications** — every disagreement and what settled it.

---

## Verification

The loop is self-verifying if these hold; check each before I deliver:

- [ ] Every reviewer returned a non-empty **"What I could not verify"** with reasoning.
- [ ] Every finding carries `file:line` + CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE + severity.
- [ ] At least one decoy-injection result is reported for any check we lean on.
- [ ] Every "exists nowhere" claim states its search scope inline.
- [ ] All four pre-registered checkpoints answered at source, independent of reviewer output.
- [ ] The shared premise was attacked by name, with a result — not merely restated.
- [ ] Every disagreement is recorded with what settled it, not averaged away.
- [ ] Nothing was pushed, committed, or posted to the PR.

Re-runnable evidence commands (all read-only, no checkout):
`git show pr/61:<path>` · `git diff 8362b3c pr/61 -- <path>` · `gh pr diff 61` ·
`gh pr checks 61` · `gh pr view 61 --json reviews,comments`

content.text:
All four checkpoints are closed, recorded here **before** any reviewer output lands so my answers can't drift toward theirs. One of my own hypotheses did not survive.

**Checkpoint 1 — Deliverable 1.** `SFCC-T150` and `SFCC-420` appear nowhere in the `pr/61` tree except inside the two `.docs/temp/` markdown files (search scope: `git grep` over the entire `pr/61` tree). No `e2e/tests/zimm/integrations/` directory exists; the whole spec dir is 3 files, all under `homepage/`. Zero `.spec.ts` files exist — 3 `.spec.js`, against an AC that specifies `.spec.ts`.

**But this is not an oversight**, and reporting it as one would be wrong. `.docs/temp/SFCC-751-implementation-spec.md:3-6` records a deliberate substitution: SFCC-420's actual work (`jobs.xml`) *lives in a different repo* (`zimmermann-sfcc`) and already shipped there — so the ticket's Deliverable 1 target is unbuildable here. The author found that during scoping and swapped in a proof-of-concept spec. The real finding is that **Jira was never amended**, so AC clauses 1 and 4, which name SFCC-T150 explicitly, remain literally unsatisfiable as written. That's a human ruling, not a code change.

**Checkpoint 2 — CONFIRMED.** `SFCC-751_mobile-header-nav-gap.spec.js:26` is a plain `test()` — no `.fixme`/`.skip`/`.fail` — ending in `expect(categoryHrefs.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)` at :42, which the author's own comment says fails today. On a `release/**` PR (`e2e_scope=full`, unscoped suite) it runs and fails by design.

**Checkpoint 3 — CONFIRMED mismatch.** The ticket specifies secret `ZEPHYR_API_TOKEN`. The code reads `ZEPHYR_API_KEY` (`zephyr-results-sync.yml:111`). Search scope: `ZEPHYR_[A-Z_]+` across `.github/workflows`, `scripts`, `.env.sample` at `pr/61` returns `ZEPHYR_API_KEY`, `ZEPHYR_API_URL`, `ZEPHYR_TESTEXECUTIONS_URL`, `ZEPHYR_PROJECT_KEY` — no `ZEPHYR_API_TOKEN`. Separately, the EU endpoint is *not enforced in code*; it comes from `secrets.ZEPHYR_API_URL`, with the DE host appearing only as a default in `.env.sample:373`.

**Checkpoint 4 — CONFIRMED, with a structural excuse.** The PR body carries an unchecked box: *"Confirm `e2e-browserstack` actually triggers on this PR and the sync workflow fires afterward — first real end-to-end run."* Both new workflows return 404 on the default branch, and `workflow_run` triggers only fire from the default branch — so Deliverable 3 is **impossible to complete before merge**. That's a genuine constraint, not negligence.

**My premise attack, partially defeated.** I predicted nothing in this chain had been demonstrated to work. The PR body shows the desktop spec *was* run against live dev across all 11 storefronts, 11/11 pass. What has never executed is Deliverable 2's runtime path — BrowserStack retrieval through Zephyr POST. That's the precise claim, and it's narrower than my premise.

**A hypothesis of mine that was wrong.** I expected the always-failing mobile spec to compound with auto-Jira-bug-filing on every release run. # PR #61 — Closed-Loop Review

## 1. Gate table

No local gates were run (your call), so this is harvested from the PR's CI plus my own scope measurements. **There is no base-vs-head baseline** — that control was forfeited deliberately.

| Gate | CI result | Files of this PR actually covered |
|---|---|---|
| Unit tests (Vitest) | pass 1m46s | **0 / 42** — ran pre-existing `overrides/` suites only |
| Storybook a11y/interaction | pass 2m57s | **0 / 42** |
| `tsc --noEmit` | not in CI | 1 / 42 (`vitest.config.ts`) |
| `lint` | not in CI | 0 / 42 (scoped `overrides/**`) |
| `audit:tokens` | not in CI | 0 / 42; exits 1 at a healthy baseline |
| Playwright E2E (localhost) | **skipping** | 0 |
| Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack) | **skipping** | 0 |
| Deploy Preview | pass 5m2s | n/a |
| File Tier & Squad Boundary | pass | passes unconditionally — no step calls `exit 1` |

Branch protection on `develop`, queried live: required checks are exactly `Storybook interaction & a11y tests`, `Unit tests (Vitest)`, `🔴 Branch Target Check`; `require_code_owner_reviews: true`, `reviews: 1`, `strict: true`.

**The PR introducing an E2E pipeline executed zero E2E tests, and its two new specs have never run in CI.**

## 2. Findings — ranked by risk

### BLOCKERS

**B1 · `Zephyr Results Sync` hard-fails on ordinary feature-branch pushes** — `zephyr-results-sync.yml:80-88`. CONFIRMED, found independently by two reviewers, chain verified by me.
`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml:41` gates the job only on `conclusion != 'cancelled'`, so it always runs and concludes `success`, short-circuiting inner steps when there's no open PR (:109), no Jira key (:127), or e2e isn't relevant (:149). The artifact upload at :177 is gated on `relevant == 'true'`, so nothing is uploaded. The sync guard then queries the job conclusion by name — and `:35` names it `Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)`, identical to qa.yml's — gets `success`, and `exit 1`.
*Failure:* first push to any `feature/**` branch before opening a PR → red `Zephyr Results Sync`. The author's comment says the identical naming makes the guard "cover e2e-browserstack-preview.yml too"; the naming matches, but they reasoned from qa.yml's *job-level* skip and missed that the preview job is never skipped.
*Fix:* move the `if:` to the job body, or upload the artifact unconditionally.
*Second defect in the same step:* no `set -e`, so a `gh api` failure leaves `CONCLUSION` empty and the guard prints "fallback is safe" and passes — the exact silent miss it exists to prevent.

**B2 · A deliberately-failing spec is being merged into the suite** — `SFCC-751_mobile-header-nav-gap.spec.js:26-42`. CONFIRMED by me and two reviewers.
Plain `test()`, no `.fixme()`/`.skip()`, ending in `expect(categoryHrefs.length).toBeGreaterThan(0)` that the author's own comment says fails today. Tagged `@SFCC-751 @homepage @p1`.
*Failure:* every `release/**` PR runs the full suite unscoped and goes red on a test that is red by design.
*Fix:* `test.fixme()` preserves the visibility the comment wants without a permanently red gate.

**B3 · The Zephyr POST omits `testCycleKey`, and the failure is green** — `zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs:178-184`. Payload verified by me: `{projectKey, testCaseKey, statusName, comment}`. `testCycleKey` appears nowhere in the `pr/61` tree (scope: full `git grep`), despite the ticket's Design Notes naming it.
*Failure:* Zephyr rejects the POST → caught at :325 → `::warning::` → `continue` → `main()` resolves → **job green, zero executions synced**. ACs 1, 3 and 4 silently unmet with a passing check.
*Fix:* send `testCycleKey`; `die()` if every POST failed.

**B4 · Secret-name mismatch against the ticket** — `zephyr-results-sync.yml:111`. CONFIRMED by me and three reviewers.
Ticket specifies `ZEPHYR_API_TOKEN`; code reads `ZEPHYR_API_KEY` everywhere. The PR's own spec doc still carries an unticked checklist item for `ZEPHYR_API_TOKEN`. If the org provisioned per the ticket, the script's `die()` fires on the first run.

### DEFECTS

**D1 · The whole sync script's failure mode is exit 0.** A `hierarchy[]` shape mismatch yields `tests: []`, loop exits, `main()` returns, exit 0 — output byte-identical to a build that legitimately ran nothing (`:144-160`). The script's own header concedes the shape has never been exercised against a real payload. Same terminal state for the `ZEPHYR_API_URL` → `/testexecutions` suffix rewrite: if the secret doesn't end in `/testcases` the `replace` at `:96` is a **no-op** and every execution POSTs to the base URL — and the ticket itself prescribes `.../v2`, the value most likely typed in.

**D2 · Auto-filed Jira Bugs are unbounded, undeduped, and provably misassigned.** No cap, dedupe, or dry-run (scope: full grep of the script). The desktop spec emits one `test()` per storefront — 11 — all carrying both required tags, so one environment-wide failure files 11 Bugs per run. A reviewer *reproduced* the assignee bug: `zephyr-results-sync.yml:45` uses bare `actions/checkout@v4` (depth 1), and on a shallow clone `git log -1 --format=%ae -- <spec>` returns the tip merge author, not the real last committer. The fallback **succeeds with the wrong answer**, so `warn()` never fires.

**D3 · PR-time E2E removed, and the stated safety net is empty.** `qa.yml` 60/61 and 75/76 change the unscopable-diff fallback from `full` to `skip`. `testing.md:191-193` justifies this by deferring to post-merge P0 gates — but **zero `.p0.spec.*` files exist at head *or* base** (scope: full `git ls-tree`), and those gates select purely by that filename pattern. This PR is its own first instance: it rewrites `BasePage.js`, inherited by every spec, and runs no Playwright at all.
*I downgraded this from a reviewer's BLOCKER* — neither E2E job is a required check, so it cannot weaken a merge gate. It removes signal, and its justification is hollow.

**D4 · `E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_VALUE` is broadcast to every origin.** `BasePage.applyExtraHeaders()` uses `page.setExtraHTTPHeaders`, which Playwright attaches to *all* page requests — so Didomi, GTM, Contentful, Emarsys and every CDN receive the access-gate secret on every run.

**D5 · A test credential pair was widened and half-committed.** `.env.sample` — `PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL` went blank→`zimm-service@zimmermann.com` and both it and `PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD` moved `scope:tier`→`scope:shared`. That file's own header states `npm run env -- push` writes **plaintext GitHub Environment Variables readable by any repo collaborator**. Found by three reviewers, verified by me. Nothing in the diff or commits explains it.

**D6 · Consent handling can silently invert.** `BasePage.js:117` replaces `getByRole('button', {name: /decline tracking/i})` with `.chakra-modal__body button:visible` then `.first()`, assuming decline precedes accept in DOM order. If that order flips, every run silently **accepts** tracking — in a Didomi-gated project. The 2-button guard checks count, not identity.

**D7 · Edge dropped from the browser matrix.** Base had 4 desktop targets; head has 3 (`chrome`, `playwright-webkit`, `playwright-firefox`). `.docs/architecture.md`'s ✅-signed-off decision still reads "Firefox + Edge (Windows 11)" — and this PR edited that exact line to fix a link while leaving the content false. It also contradicts the signed-off "current − 2" device policy explicitly.

**D8 · Relevance check fails open onto a paid BrowserStack run.** Four triggers, including `e2e-scope` artifact `retention-days: 1` — any Deploy Preview re-run after 24h fails open, unacknowledged anywhere.

**D9 · Tier-guard consolidation breaks step independence.** Three jobs merged into one with no `continue-on-error`/`if: always()`; a throwing `github-script` step now skips the Squad A/B detection steps that previously ran as separate jobs. The job's comment asserts the opposite. *Its other claim — that only `🔴 Branch Target Check` is required — I verified as correct.*

**D10 · `browserstack.yml` is invisible to the tier guard.** No `browserstack` entry at base or head. Pre-existing for the dotted name, but this PR renames the file, re-asserts its Tier 1 status, routes it in CODEOWNERS, *and* restructures the guard — so its own premise makes this a defect. A full enumeration also found 7 `frozenFiles.md` Tier 1 paths unmatched by the guard (including all 5 real files under `overrides/app/ssr/`, because `overrides/app/ssr.*` doesn't cross `/`) and 2 guard patterns absent from `frozenFiles.md`.

### Governance — enforced, and will block merge

12 Tier 1 paths are touched. With `require_code_owner_reviews: true` confirmed live, these are real gates, not advisory:
- **Hard Rule 8** — `vitest.config.ts` is named explicitly as never-modify and gains a coverage block. The only justification is a source comment by the change's author.
- **Hard Rule 7** — `@vitest/coverage-v8` added; no integration-team approval in the PR body or any of the 20 commit messages.
- **Hard Rule 9** — the `.browserstack.yml` deletion is not mentioned in the PR body at all.

**Against the ticket:** Deliverable 1 was *substituted, not skipped* — SFCC-420's work lives in the `zimmermann-sfcc` repo and already shipped, recorded at `.docs/temp/SFCC-751-implementation-spec.md:3-6`. Sound engineering, but Jira was never amended, so ACs 1 and 4 (which name SFCC-T150) are unsatisfiable as written. Deliverable 3 is not done and is **structurally impossible pre-merge** — `workflow_run` workflows only fire from the default branch; both return 404 there today. **HAR attachment (Deliverable 2) is absent entirely** — zero hits tree-wide.

### Tail (low risk, per your steer)

Stale/false comments in files this PR edited: `qa.yml:179-181` describes Jira-key scoping that no longer exists and `jira_keys` now has zero consumers; `deploy-preview.yml:424` and `computeBuildName.mjs:11-12` both name the wrong caller; six places still promise the deleted full-suite fallback; `AGENTS.md:57,78` plus the regenerated `copilot-instructions.md` name a `tier1-guard` job that no longer exists. Spec filenames omit the `.p1.` priority infix that `playwright.config.js` uses for P0 selection. `.docs/temp/` ships a superseded brief that production code cites, containing an ownership claim (`@hsemp`) that appears nowhere else in the repo. 21 of 42 paths have no CODEOWNERS entry.

## 3. What nobody verified

- **Live GitHub config**, except branch protection which I closed: whether `ZEPHYR_API_KEY`, `ZEPHYR_API_URL`, `JIRA_AUTOMATION_*`, `E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_*` and the `test` env's `RETAIL_APP_HOME` exist at all; whether `ZEPHYR_API_URL`'s real value is the DE `/testcases` form; whether `environment: test` carries required reviewers that would block both E2E jobs on manual approval. **These are the highest-value pre-merge human checks.**
- **BrowserStack's real payload shape and tag field** — no credentials; D1 is "what happens if", not "what does".
- **Whether Zephyr v2 hard-rejects a missing `testCycleKey`** — the omission is confirmed, the rejection is reasoned.
- **BrowserStack device catalogue** for iPhone 17 / Galaxy S26 / Pixel 11 — the config concedes these are unverified.
- **Whether Test Observability collapses the 6 platforms per title** — decides whether D2 files 11 or up to 66 Bugs per run. The 11 floor is proved.
- **Lead QA sign-off** on the `.feature` — absent from repo, PR body and all commits, but may exist in Jira/Confluence. No `.feature` exists for the mobile spec at all.
- **The forfeited baseline** — with no base-vs-head gate run, inherited-vs-introduced separation rests on reading, not measurement.
- **R1's angle (CI control-flow regression tracing) is still outstanding.**

## 4. My adjudications

- **Two wrong premises I injected, both caught by reviewers rather than by me.** I labelled `deploy-preview.yml` "(new)" in all four briefs — it's `M`, modified. And I told them "a skipped required check counts as passing", which let them infer the E2E jobs were gating; branch protection shows they never were. The first was refused by a reviewer; the second I caught only by querying the API myself.
- **Downgraded** a BLOCKER to DEFECT (D3): the reviewer's severity rested on merge-gate weakening, which the branch-protection data refutes. The finding survives on different grounds — the empty P0 safety net.
- **Overreach downgraded:** a reviewer called two same-dated "live-verified" claims a flat contradiction — one asserting an 11-pass BrowserStack build, one asserting zero builds exist. They're reconcilable: this PR renames the project `Zimmermann-PWA`→`Zim Project`, and the "zero builds" claim is scoped to "this account's *configured* project". I dropped the contradiction framing but kept the substance, because a second reviewer independently found the related real problem — an in-code claim citing *local Playwright* evidence (`test_tags`) for a *BrowserStack API* field (`details.tags`).
- **A hypothesis of mine that was wrong:** I expected the always-red mobile spec to compound with auto-Jira-filing on every release run. It can't — `:304` does `if (!zephyrKey) continue` before any write, and that spec carries no `@zephyr:` tag.
- **My premise attack was partially defeated.** I predicted nothing in the chain had been demonstrated to work. The desktop spec *was* run against live dev, 11/11 across all storefronts. The precise claim is narrower: **Deliverable 2's runtime path — BrowserStack retrieval through Zephyr POST — has never executed.**
- **Resolved in the PR's favour:** the `.browserstack.yml`→`browserstack.yml` rename correctly re-covers Tier 1; the AI-config mirrors were proved byte-identical by regeneration; the tier-guard pattern lists are byte-identical base→head; `testSuite: e2e/tests/zimm` scope is preserved; and the sync script's non-terminal-status guard deliberately prevents false Zephyr failures.

**Bottom line:** the architecture is sound and unusually well-documented, but B1 breaks CI for every developer on ordinary pushes, B2 puts a permanently-red test in the release suite, and B3/D1 mean the pipeline's dominant failure mode is a green check with nothing synced. Nothing has been posted to the PR.

content.text:
R1 was worth the wait — it invalidates my headline finding and one of my own premises. Corrections first.

---

# Revised Report — corrections to what I sent

## The frame went stale mid-review

**The PR head moved while we were reviewing it.** I fetched `74e2b82` at Stage 0; the live head is now `5fe247c1` — a 21st commit pushed 2026-08-26T00:59Z touching 5 files. R2, R3 and R4 all reviewed the stale ref. R1 detected the drift itself, fetched the new commit, and marked which of its findings it affects. That's the single most valuable thing any of the four did.

**My headline BLOCKER B1 is already fixed.** The new commit says so explicitly:

> *Fix a real regression in zephyr-results-sync.yml's build-name guard: it checked job-level conclusion, which would fail the sync job on every normal develop PR that legitimately skips BrowserStack (the common case). Now checks the specific step's conclusion instead.*

CodeRabbit flagged it 2026-08-26. So R3 and R4 independently found a real bug that the author had already fixed hours earlier. Also fixed in that commit: the `protected-file-guard.yml` script-injection vector R4 flagged as residual, the silent test-tier fallback behind R4's D4, and `npm install` → `npm ci --ignore-scripts`.

## A third wrong premise I injected — and it inverts a finding

I told all four reviewers, in the Stage 0 trap audit, that *"Playwright `--grep` with no match exits 0 '0 passed'."* **That is false.** R1 refuted it from the installed runner, `playwright@1.60.0`, `node_modules/playwright/lib/runner/index.js:6003-6011`:

```js
if (options.failOnLoadErrors && !testRun.rootSuite?.allTests().length
    && !testRun.options.passWithNoTests && ...) {
  throw new Error(`No tests found`);
}
```

`passWithNoTests` is set nowhere in `playwright.config.js` or `.github/workflows/` (verified). Zero-match **throws** → non-zero exit. My premise came from the Stage 0 gate inventory and I passed it on unverified.

# Revised BLOCKERS

**New B1 · Every develop PR will get a red BrowserStack Preview run after merge.** CONFIRMED at live head.
`e2e-browserstack-preview.yml:241-242` builds `--grep "$GREP"` from any `SFCC-\d+` in the PR title, body or branch — **no zero-match guard, no `--pass-with-no-tests`**. Across all of `e2e/tests/zimm` exactly **one** story key has a tagged spec:

```
SMOKE-homepage-load.spec.js              (none)
SFCC-751_header-nav-site-prefix.spec.js  @SFCC-751
SFCC-751_mobile-header-nav-gap.spec.js   @SFCC-751
```

This repo's branch convention is `feature/SFCC-NNN_…` — your own current branch is `feature/SFCC-89_pdp-static-product-info`. Any such PR yields `--grep "@SFCC-89"` → zero match → `No tests found` → red job. And `testing.md:372-373` **still asserts at the live head** that this is "a free no-op, not a failure" — a Tier 1 rules doc documenting the opposite of the runner's behaviour, with code built on the wrong assumption.
*Fix:* add `--pass-with-no-tests`, or guard the grep result, and correct the doc.

**B2 · The deliberately-red spec, and the sequence around it.** CONFIRMED, with CI evidence.
R1 recovered the causal chain from run history: run `32814990913` (commit `fd082b4`, `e2e_scope=full`) ran 16 tests → **15 passed, 1 failed**, the failure being `SFCC-751_mobile-header-nav-gap.spec.js:42` across all three attempts. **The very next commit, `fb1bd6c` — "fix(ci): skip e2e-localhost on unscoped develop PRs instead of running everything" — flipped `full`→`skip`.** `Playwright E2E (localhost)` has been skipped on every run since; across 20 runs on this branch it is failure ×7, cancelled ×1, skipped ×12, **success ×0**.
I'm stating the sequence as fact and drawing no conclusion about intent — but a reviewer needs to see it, because the change is presented purely as a CI-minutes optimisation and its observed effect was to turn the only red job green without fixing the test. R1 also built the decoy: a PR touching only `overrides/app/pages/home/**` still resolves to `e2e_scope=homepage`, still matches `@homepage`, and still goes red. The skip is not blanket immunity.

**B3 · `testCycleKey` omitted; the failure is green.** Unchanged — payload verified by me as `{projectKey, testCaseKey, statusName, comment}`.

**B4 · Secret name `ZEPHYR_API_KEY` vs the ticket's `ZEPHYR_API_TOKEN`.** Unchanged. R1 confirms both `ZEPHYR_API_KEY` and `ZEPHYR_API_URL` exist as repo secrets, so the *names* are provisioned as coded — but the ticket's contract is still the wrong one.

# Additions from R1

- **The desktop/mobile split does not work on BrowserStack.** From real run logs: the mobile spec executed under `OSX Sonoma` and `Windows 11`. `browserstack-node-sdk` cross-multiplies Playwright projects by platforms — `--grep @SFCC-751` matched 12 local tests and produced **60** remote instances. The `testIgnore` reasoning `testing.md` is built on holds locally and not on the only surface the Zephyr sync ever reads. With 6 platforms at `parallelsPerPlatform: 1` on a 1-concurrent-session plan: 72 sequential sessions against a 25-minute timeout on the develop path, 96 against 30 minutes on release.
- **`Unit tests (Vitest)` — one of only three required checks — can fail on a GitHub comment API error.** `qa.yml:285-350` has `if: always()` and no `continue-on-error`, so a `listComments`/`createComment` 403/5xx fails the job. New fragility coupled to a real merge gate. One-line fix.
- **`npm ci --ignore-scripts` is undercut seconds later.** `browserstack-node-sdk` is in neither `package.json` nor `package-lock.json`; it's invoked by bare `npx` with `BROWSERSTACK_*`, `E2E_*` and `JIRA_*` in scope — an unpinned download-and-execute immediately after the hardened install.
- **Seven E2E secrets referenced in CI do not exist** (`PWA_E2E_USER_*`, four `E2E_*_SKU`, `E2E_FIXTURE_ORDER_NUMBER`) — verified against the 11 repo secrets and the `test` environment. Latent today, fatal for the first auth or PDP spec.
- **The build name is run-invariant**, and `findBuild()` takes `builds[0]` with no ordering guarantee — so the sync can attach a *stale* build's results. The `unknown-<key>` fallback is worse: constant across every run.
- **The 11 per-site tests all share `@zephyr:SFCC-T285`** — so one run posts 11 executions against a single Zephyr case, and a failing run files up to 11 Jira Bugs with no dedupe.

**R1 also closed two things in the PR's favour**, having tried to falsify both: MRT preview contention is a non-issue (per-branch concurrency group *and* per-branch target slug), and the tier-guard check rename will not deadlock the merge (none of the three removed check names is in `develop`'s required set).

# Revised adjudications

- **Retracted:** my B1. Real when found, fixed before I reported it. Two reviewers found it independently and both were right about the stale ref.
- **Three premises I injected were wrong** — `deploy-preview.yml` mislabelled "(new)", "skipped required checks count as passing" applied to jobs that were never required, and the `--grep` exit-code claim. Reviewers caught the first and third; I caught the second. The `--grep` one is the serious miss: it pointed four reviewers away from what is now the top blocker.
- **Process lesson worth keeping:** Stage 0's frame needs re-checking at Stage 2, not just recorded at Stage 1. Had R1 not done it unprompted, I'd have handed you a stale headline.

**Bottom line, revised:** the fixed guard removes the immediate breakage, but the `--grep` zero-match takes its place and is worse — it fires on nearly every future PR, and the Tier 1 rules doc documents it backwards. B2's sequence, and the fact that this PR has 0 successful BrowserStack runs out of 20 attempts, are what I'd put in front of a human before merge. Nothing posted to the PR.

content.text:
## What the PR is trying to build

A robot that: runs the website's tests on real phones and browsers → writes the results into the team's test-tracking tool → and files a bug ticket automatically when something fails.

Good idea. Well documented. The wiring has problems.

## What we found, plainly

**The safety checks that passed on this PR checked almost nothing.** All the automated checks are pointed at one folder. This PR doesn't touch that folder. So the green ticks cover 1 file out of 42. The green wasn't a green light — it was a light that isn't wired to anything.

**The robot has never once worked.** 20 attempts on this branch. Zero successes. The part that talks to the tracking tool has literally never run, because that kind of workflow only switches on *after* it's merged. So merging is a leap of faith by design.

**There's a test written to fail on purpose.** It's flagging a genuinely missing feature — fine idea — but it isn't marked "expected to fail," so it just looks broken. It'll turn release builds red.

**And here's the uncomfortable bit:** the moment that test made the build red, the very next commit switched off the thing that runs the tests. The commit is described as a cost saving. It may well have been. But that's the order events happened, and someone should look at it.

**The biggest one:** the robot picks which tests to run by matching a ticket number, like `SFCC-89`. Almost no tests have ticket numbers attached. When it finds nothing to run, the tool doesn't shrug — it errors out. So after this merges, nearly every future PR gets a red mark for no reason. The team's own written rules say the opposite happens.

**When the robot fails, it says it succeeded.** It's missing a required field when it writes results, so those writes will likely bounce — and the code catches the error, shrugs, and reports success. Silent failure with a green tick.

## What I got wrong

I gave the four reviewers three incorrect facts. They caught two; I caught one. The third was the worst — it steered them away from what turned out to be the top problem.

And the thing I called the single biggest blocker had **already been fixed** while we were reviewing. The author pushed an update mid-review and I didn't re-check. One reviewer noticed on its own and re-verified against the current code — otherwise I'd have handed you a stale headline.

## What I'd do

Don't merge on the green ticks. Get the ticket-matching crash fixed, mark the deliberate failure as deliberate, and ask about that commit sequence.

## The one-sentence version

The new BrowserStack job asks Playwright for "all tests tagged with this PR's ticket number," almost no tests have tags yet, and Playwright treats "found nothing" as an error rather than a shrug — so the job turns red.

## Walk it through on your own branch

You're on `feature/SFCC-89_pdp-static-product-info`. After this PR merges, you push. Then:

1. The workflow scans your PR title, body and branch name for a ticket number. It finds **SFCC-89**.
2. It builds a filter: *"only run tests labelled `@SFCC-89`."*
3. It hands that to Playwright: `playwright test e2e/tests/zimm --grep "@SFCC-89"`.
4. Playwright looks through all three spec files. Two are labelled `@SFCC-751`. One has no label at all. **Nothing matches `@SFCC-89`.**
5. Playwright doesn't say "fine, nothing to do." It throws `No tests found` and exits with an error code.
6. GitHub sees an error code → **red X on your PR**.

You didn't do anything wrong. Your PR has nothing to do with BrowserStack. It goes red anyway.

Think of it like sending someone to the library for "every book tagged SFCC-89." There are none. Instead of coming back and saying "none in stock," they file an incident report.

## Why nobody caught it

Playwright *can* be told to treat "no matches" as fine — there's a `--pass-with-no-tests` flag for exactly this. It isn't set anywhere, and the config doesn't enable it either.

Worse, the project's own testing rules file — `testing.md`, a Tier 1 governance doc — states the opposite in writing:

> "…`--grep` matches zero tests and Playwright reports 'no tests found' … a free no-op, **not a failure**"

So anyone reading the docs would reasonably build exactly what was built. The code isn't careless; it's faithfully implementing a documented behaviour that the tool doesn't actually have. I checked the installed Playwright source directly, and the throw is right there.

I'll add: I gave all four reviewers that same wrong belief in their briefs, because I'd taken it from the docs too. Three of them worked around it. One went and read the runner source.

## Why it matters

It hits **almost every future PR**, not an edge case, because this repo names branches `feature/SFCC-NNN_…` — so there's virtually always a ticket number to find, and virtually never a matching tagged test. Only one ticket in the entire repo has tagged specs today.

The practical damage is the boy-who-cried-wolf problem: a check that's red on every PR gets ignored within a week, and then it's red for a *real* reason and nobody looks.

## The fix

Small — roughly a one-line change plus a doc correction:

- Add `--pass-with-no-tests` to the Playwright call, **or** check whether the filter matched anything before running at all
- Fix `testing.md:372-373` so it describes what Playwright actually does

Worth flagging to the author as a doc-first bug rather than a coding mistake — the doc is what led them here, and it'll lead the next person the same way if it isn't corrected.
