content.text:
## The one-sentence version

Someone added a test that is *designed* to fail — as a deliberate reminder that a feature is missing — and the very next commit switched off the job that was running it. CI went green without the test being fixed.

## The two pieces

**Piece one: a test written to fail on purpose.**

`SFCC-751_mobile-header-nav-gap.spec.js` checks that the mobile menu contains category links. It doesn't — that feature hasn't been built yet. The author knew, and says so in the file:

> *"Expected to fail today: the mobile drawer currently has no category navigation content at all… This test exists to make that gap visible in CI rather than silently untested."*

That's a reasonable instinct — a tripwire so the gap can't be forgotten. The problem is it's wired to the wrong lamp. Playwright has `test.fixme()` for exactly this: it records "known broken, don't count it against us" and shows up in reports without turning the build red. This used a plain failing assertion instead, which is indistinguishable from a genuine break.

**Piece two: the job that ran it got switched off.**

Here's the timeline, straight from the run history:

| | |
|---|---|
| Commit `fd082b4` | E2E runs the full suite → **16 tests, 15 passed, 1 failed** — the failure is that mobile spec, on all three attempts. Job goes **red**. |
| Commit `fb1bd6c` (**the very next one**) | *"fix(ci): skip e2e-localhost on unscoped develop PRs instead of running everything"* — flips the fallback from `full` to `skip`. |
| Every run since | `Playwright E2E (localhost)` = **skipped**. |

Across all 20 runs on this branch: 7 failures, 1 cancelled, 12 skipped, **0 successes**.

## What I am and am not saying

I'm reporting the sequence as fact. I am **not** claiming anyone silenced a test on purpose, and I don't think you should assume it either.

The innocent reading is genuinely plausible: running the whole E2E suite on every PR is expensive, narrowing it is a legitimate optimisation, there's a written rationale for it, and the two changes landing back-to-back could be coincidence.

But a reviewer has to see the sequence, because the change was presented *purely* as a CI-cost optimisation, and its observable effect was to make the only red job green without touching the failing test. Those two facts sit uncomfortably together, and only the author can say which it was. That's a question for them, not a verdict from me.

## The part that actually bites

The test isn't hidden — it's only hidden *on this PR*. R1 deliberately constructed the cases that should still run it, and they do:

- Any **release branch** PR → runs the full suite → red
- Any PR touching only the homepage area → matches the test's `@homepage` tag → red
- Any PR mentioning **SFCC-751** → matches its ticket tag → red

So this surfaces later, on a release branch, at the worst possible moment — when someone is trying to ship and has no context on why a test they've never seen is failing.

## The fix

Two independent things, both small:

- Change the spec to `test.fixme()`. Keeps the visibility the author wants, stops the red.
- Review the `full`→`skip` change **on its own merits**, as a separate decision. It may well be the right call — but it's a policy change about how much testing every PR in the repo gets, and it shouldn't ride in on a QA-tooling ticket without being discussed as such.

content.text:
You were right to push, and the answer is more precise than what I reported — in one place it exonerates the PR, in another it makes things worse.

## Your specific question: was the E2E skip caused by this PR?

**Yes — verified, not assumed.** 20 of 21 commits would have run the full suite under base logic and skip under this PR's. Only the docs-only commit would have skipped either way. So it is not "nothing relevant changed."

**But the PR has a legitimate case here that I under-reported.** Those commits count as e2e-relevant mainly because `qa.yml`, `browserstack.yml` and `computeBuildName.mjs` are themselves *in* the `e2e` group. Under base logic, editing a workflow file triggered a full browser suite. That's real over-triggering and a fair thing to want fixed. R1 framed the change as suspicious; on the evidence it has a defensible rationale.

**The damage is to normal PRs, and yours is the proof.** Your `feature/SFCC-89` branch: 25 changed files, all 25 e2e-relevant (all under `overrides/`), none in the homepage allow-list → base logic `full`, this PR `skip`. An ordinary PDP component PR loses its entire PR-time E2E run.

## And the two findings compound — for a reason nobody spotted

The two gates read **different fields**. `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml:165` does `jq -r '.e2e'` — it reads `e2e`, *not* `e2e_scope`. So on your branch:

| | gates on | result |
|---|---|---|
| Playwright E2E (localhost) | `e2e_scope` → `skip` | **silently off** |
| BrowserStack Preview | `e2e` → `true` | **runs** → `--grep "@SFCC-89"` → zero match → **red** |

One gate honours the scope decision, the other ignores it. You get no local E2E signal *and* a red remote job. That's the worst combination, and it's a two-line inconsistency, not a design flaw.

## Re-adjudication of everything I flagged

| Finding | Verdict after probing | Change |
|---|---|---|
| **B1 `--grep` zero-match** | Strengthened — relevance keys off `e2e`, so it fires on any e2e-relevant PR with a ticket key | ↑ |
| **B2a deliberately-red spec** | Stands. Independent of the scope change | = |
| **B2b scope change causation** | Confirmed 20/21, but with a legitimate over-triggering rationale I'd omitted | ↓ severity, ↑ precision |
| **B3 `testCycleKey`** | Omission CONFIRMED; runtime rejection still only PLAUSIBLE. I let those blur | ↓ |
| **B4 `ZEPHYR_API_KEY` vs `TOKEN`** | **Was overstated.** R1 verified both secrets exist under the *code's* names. Nothing breaks — the *ticket* is stale, not the code | **BLOCKER → NOTE** |
| **D2 Jira assignee** | R4 and R1 disagreed; both right. Pre-merge the spec isn't in develop's tree → unassigned. Post-merge → shallow clone → wrong assignee | refined |
| **D8 relevance fail-open** | Re-confirmed at live head (`:165-170`) | = |
| **D9 guard consolidation** | Script-injection half **fixed** at live head; step-independence half stands | partial ↓ |
| D1, D3–D7, D10 | Unchanged | = |

## What this says about the method

Three of my findings moved under scrutiny, and one was flatly wrong — B4, where I reasoned "if the secret were provisioned per the ticket it would die" and never checked whether it was. R1 did check. That's the same failure mode I'd been penalising in reviewers: a correct chain of reasoning from an unverified premise.

The pattern across this whole review is consistent — every error, mine and the reviewers', came from **inheriting a claim instead of testing it**: the stale head, the `--grep` exit code, the "(new)" file label, the required-check assumption, the secret name. Not one came from bad analysis. That's the argument for exactly what you just made me do.

**Revised bottom line:** B1 is the finding to lead with — it's real, it hits ordinary PRs, and it's a small fix. B2a (`test.fixme()`) is a one-line fix. B2b deserves to be discussed as a policy decision on its own merits rather than treated as a red flag. B4 comes off the blocker list entirely.

content.text:
# Why each item was flagged — plain language

I've grouped by *kind of problem* rather than severity, because the reason for flagging is what you asked about.

---

## Group 1 — Will break CI for everyone

### B1 · The `--grep` zero-match
**What it does:** The new job asks Playwright for "tests tagged with this PR's ticket number." Only one ticket in the whole repo has tagged tests.
**Why flagged:** Playwright treats "found nothing" as an error, not a shrug. So the job errors out.
**What breaks:** Nearly every future PR gets a red X for no reason. Red-on-everything means people stop looking, and then it's red for a *real* reason and nobody notices.

### R1's find · A required check can fail on a cosmetic error
**What it does:** After running unit tests, the job posts a coverage comment on the PR.
**Why flagged:** If GitHub's comment API hiccups (rate limit, brief outage), the comment step fails — and because it isn't marked "allowed to fail," it drags the whole job down with it.
**What breaks:** `Unit tests (Vitest)` is one of only three checks that actually block merging. So a cosmetic comment failure blocks a merge. One-line fix.

### The `@SFCC-75` / `@SFCC-751` collision
**What it does:** Matches ticket tags by text search, unanchored.
**Why flagged:** "SFCC-75" is contained inside "SFCC-751". A PR for ticket 75 would drag in ticket 751's tests.
**What breaks:** Nothing today — but it's a landmine that gets more likely as more tests get tagged.

---

## Group 2 — Fails silently (the dangerous kind)

These are the ones I'd worry about most. A loud failure gets fixed. A quiet one gets trusted.

### B3 · The Zephyr upload is missing a required field
**What it does:** Sends `{project, testCase, status, comment}` to Zephyr. The ticket's own notes say it also needs `testCycleKey`.
**Why flagged:** If Zephyr rejects the upload, the code logs a warning and *carries on*. The job finishes green.
**What breaks:** Your dashboard says "sync succeeded." Zephyr has nothing in it. You'd only discover this by going and looking manually — which defeats the entire point of building the pipeline.
**Honesty note:** I'm confident the field is missing. I'm *not* certain Zephyr rejects without it — that needs one API call to confirm.

### D1 · If BrowserStack's data looks different than expected, you get a clean "nothing to sync"
**What it does:** The script expects BrowserStack's response in a specific shape. Its own comments admit that shape has never been tested against real data.
**Why flagged:** If the shape is wrong, the code finds zero tests, prints "0 tests", and exits successfully — *identical output to a run where nothing legitimately happened*.
**What breaks:** You cannot tell "everything passed and synced" apart from "the parser is broken." Same message, same green tick.

### D1b · The URL rewrite can silently miss
**What it does:** Takes your Zephyr URL and swaps `/testcases` on the end for `/testexecutions`.
**Why flagged:** If your URL doesn't end in `/testcases`, the swap does nothing and it posts to the wrong address. And the ticket itself tells you to use a URL *without* that ending.
**What breaks:** Every upload goes to the wrong place, each one warns, the job stays green.

### The build name never changes between runs
**What it does:** Names each BrowserStack build after the ticket, with no run number.
**Why flagged:** Every run for the same ticket produces the same name. When the sync script looks up "the build with this name," it grabs the first match with no guarantee of which.
**What breaks:** You could sync *yesterday's* results and believe they're today's.

---

## Group 3 — Leaks and over-sharing

### D4 · A secret header is sent to every website the page touches
**What it does:** Attaches an access-gate secret to requests so tests can reach the protected test environment.
**Why flagged:** The Playwright function used attaches it to **every** request the page makes — not just yours. Your storefront loads Didomi, Google Tag Manager, Contentful, Emarsys, CDNs.
**What breaks:** All of those third parties receive your access secret, on every test run. Nothing "breaks" — that's why it needs flagging, it's invisible.

### D5 · A test account's email was committed, and its sharing setting widened
**What it does:** `.env.sample` now contains `zimm-service@zimmermann.com` where it used to be blank, and both the email and its password field moved from "per-environment" to "shared."
**Why flagged:** That file's own header says the "shared" setting publishes values as **plaintext, readable by any repo collaborator**. And an email sitting directly above a password field is half a login.
**What breaks:** Widens who can see a test credential. Unexplained in the PR — might simply be an accident.

### D8 · When it can't tell whether to run, it runs (and bills you)
**What it does:** Checks a small file to decide whether a BrowserStack run is needed.
**Why flagged:** If that file is missing or unreadable, it defaults to **yes, run**. And the file is deleted after 24 hours.
**What breaks:** Re-running a build a day later triggers a full paid browser run that wasn't needed — on a plan that only allows one session at a time, so it's slow too.

### The `npm ci --ignore-scripts` hardening is undone seconds later
**What it does:** Installs dependencies safely, blocking packages from running setup code.
**Why flagged:** The very next line runs `npx browserstack-node-sdk` — a package that's in *neither* `package.json` nor the lockfile. So it downloads an unpinned package from the internet and executes it, with all your secrets in scope.
**What breaks:** The security fix is real but it's bypassed immediately. Worth knowing the protection is thinner than it reads.

---

## Group 4 — Test coverage quietly lost

### B2a · A test that's *designed* to fail
**What it does:** Asserts the mobile menu has category links. It doesn't — that feature isn't built.
**Why flagged:** The author did this on purpose, as a reminder. Good instinct, wrong tool — Playwright has `test.fixme()` for "known missing," which records it without turning the build red.
**What breaks:** Red builds on release branches, at the worst moment, for someone with no context.

### B2b · Normal PRs now run no browser tests
**What it does:** Changed the fallback from "run everything" to "run nothing" when a PR's changes span more than one area.
**Why flagged:** I verified this against your own branch: 25 files, all e2e-relevant, none in the one allow-listed area → you'd get **zero** browser tests where you previously got the full suite.
**Genuine counter-argument:** editing a workflow file used to trigger a full browser suite, which is wasteful. The author had a real problem to solve. **This one is a policy decision, not a bug** — it just shouldn't ride in unannounced on a QA-tooling ticket.

### The desktop/mobile split doesn't work where it matters
**What it does:** Splits tests into `desktop/` and `mobile/` folders so each runs on the right browser only.
**Why flagged:** That works when you run locally. On BrowserStack, the tool multiplies every test across every platform — R1 found log evidence of the *mobile* test running on macOS and Windows. 12 tests became 60 remote runs.
**What breaks:** The whole design rationale written into the rules doc doesn't hold on the only system that feeds Zephyr. Also 60–96 sequential runs against a 25-minute timeout.

### D7 · Edge browser silently dropped
**What it does:** The browser list went from 4 desktop browsers to 3.
**Why flagged:** Edge is gone with no replacement, and `.docs/architecture.md` — a *signed-off* decision — still says "Firefox + Edge." This PR edited that exact line to fix a link and left the now-false text.
**What breaks:** You believe you're testing Edge. You aren't.

---

## Group 5 — Process and governance

### 12 protected files, one package added
**Why flagged:** Your own rules mark these as needing named-owner sign-off — `vitest.config.ts` is specifically listed as "never modify," and adding any package needs integration-team approval. Neither approval appears in the PR body or any of the 21 commits.
**Why it's real:** I confirmed GitHub enforces code-owner review on `develop`, so this genuinely blocks merge. Not a formality.

### The ticket asked for a different test entirely
**Why flagged:** SFCC-751 asks for a Global-e integration spec tagged `SFCC-T150`. What shipped is a homepage nav spec tagged `SFCC-T285`.
**Important context:** this was **deliberate and well-reasoned** — the author found that SFCC-420's work lives in a different repo and already shipped, so the requested test was unbuildable here. That's good engineering. The gap is that **Jira was never updated**, so the ticket's acceptance criteria can never be met as written.

### End-to-end validation never happened
**Why flagged:** The ticket's third deliverable is "prove the whole chain works." It hasn't been proven — 0 successful BrowserStack runs out of 20 attempts.
**Important context:** this is **structurally impossible before merge**. The workflows only activate once they're on the default branch. So this isn't negligence — it's a real constraint that means merging is inherently a leap, and someone should plan an immediate post-merge check.

### HAR files not attached
**Why flagged:** The ticket explicitly requires attaching a HAR (a network recording) for debugging. There is no HAR anywhere in the code.
**What breaks:** Nothing — but a requirement was dropped without a written note saying so.

---

## Group 6 — Things I flagged that turned out fine

Worth showing, because a review that only ever finds problems isn't a review.

- **`ZEPHYR_API_KEY` vs `ZEPHYR_API_TOKEN`** — I called this a blocker. R1 checked and both secrets **exist** under the names the code uses. Nothing breaks; the *ticket* is out of date. My error: I reasoned from an unverified assumption.
- **The `.browserstack.yml` rename** — I worried it dropped the file's protected status. The author handled it properly in both places.
- **Preview deploys clobbering each other** — R1 tried to break this and couldn't. Per-branch isolation is correct.
- **The check rename deadlocking merges** — verified safe.
- **The auto-Jira-bug flood hitting the always-red test** — I predicted this; it can't happen, there's a guard that stops it.

---

**If you only act on three things:** add `--pass-with-no-tests` (B1), change the failing spec to `test.fixme()` (B2a), and get someone to confirm whether Zephyr needs `testCycleKey` before merge (B3) — because that last one is the difference between a working pipeline and a green tick over an empty dashboard.

**PROVEN** (show evidence) · **PARTIALLY PROVEN** (mechanism proven, consequence doesn't follow — say which part) · **UNPROVEN** (say what would settle it) · **REFUTED** (show why).

=== CLAIMS TO TEST ===

**C16.** `e2e/support/pages/BasePage.js` applies `E2E_EXTRA_HEADER_NAME`/`_VALUE` via Playwright's `page.setExtraHTTPHeaders()`, which attaches the header to EVERY request the page makes — including third-party origins (Didomi, GTM, Contentful, Emarsys, CDNs) — not only the storefront origin. So an access-gate secret is transmitted to third parties on every run.
**Attack it:** (a) verify the actual API used at live head — is it `setExtraHTTPHeaders` on the page/context, or `route()`-scoped, or set per-`goto`? And `.env.sample`'s own header states that `npm run env -- push shared` writes values as plaintext GitHub Environment **Variables** readable by repo collaborators.

Also check `scripts/switchEnv.mjs` for whether `scope:shared` keys are actually pushed and as Variables vs Secrets. Is the email a "secret" by this repo's own definition?

**C18.** `browserstack.yml` at `pr/61-live` removes Edge with no replacement (base `.browserstack.yml` had chrome/safari/firefox/edge; head has chrome/playwright-webkit/playwright-firefox + 3 real mobile devices), AND `.docs/architecture.md` at live head still states the desktop matrix includes Edge, AND this PR edited that architecture.md line without correcting the content.
**Attack it:** is `playwright-webkit`/`playwright-firefox` a rename of the same coverage? Can Playwright even drive Edge on BrowserStack (check whether an `msedge` channel option exists in this setup)? If Edge is technically unsupported for Playwright runs, the finding changes from "coverage silently dropped" to "coverage was never achievable this way" — determine which.

**C19.** At `pr/61-live`, `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml`'s relevance check sets `relevant=true` unless an `e2e-scope.json` artifact exists AND its `.e2e` field is `"false"` — i.e. it FAILS OPEN onto a paid BrowserStack run when the artifact is missing/unreadable. And `qa.yml` uploads that artifact with `retention-days: 1`, so a Deploy Preview re-run >24h later fails open.
Verify both, at live head (the newer commit touched this file — check whether the fail-open was changed).

**C20 — verify a claim made from CI logs.** A prior reviewer claimed that under `browserstack-node-sdk`, the SDK cross-multiplies Playwright projects by configured platforms, so the MOBILE spec executed on `OSX Sonoma` and `Windows 11`, and `--grep @SFCC-751` matching 12 local tests produced 60 BrowserStack instances. Evidence cited: run `32805482849`, job `97674692941`.
**Verify independently** via `gh api` / `gh run view --log` for that run. Does the log actually show that? If you cannot retrieve the log, say so — do NOT accept the claim on the prior reviewer's word.

**C21.** `browserstack-node-sdk` appears in NEITHER `package.json` nor `package-lock.json` at `pr/61-live`, yet is invoked via bare `npx` in the workflows — so the `npm ci --ignore-scripts` hardening added in the newest commit is followed by an unpinned registry download-and-execute in the same job with secrets in scope. Verify each part; state search scope inline.

**C22.** `BasePage.js` at `pr/61-live` replaced an accessible-name selector (`getByRole('button', {name: /decline tracking/i})` at base) with a CSS class selector (`.chakra-modal__body button:visible`) and takes `.first()`, assuming decline precedes accept in DOM order — so if that order ever flips, the suite silently ACCEPTS tracking.
**Attack it:** is there any guard that verifies the button's identity (text/aria) rather than just counting? Is the base version really what I claim? Does anything downstream assert consent state?

**C23.** Seven E2E secrets referenced in CI do not exist: `PWA_E2E_USER_EMAIL`, `PWA_E2E_USER_PASSWORD`, `E2E_STANDARD_PRODUCT_SKU`, `E2E_VARIANT_PRODUCT_SKU`, `E2E_OOS_PRODUCT_SKU`, `E2E_SALE_PRODUCT_SKU`, `E2E_FIXTURE_ORDER_NUMBER`. Verify via `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/actions/secrets` and the relevant environment secrets endpoints. Note secret VALUES are not readable but NAMES are. Also determine whether this is pre-existing (check base) or introduced by this PR.

=== OUTPUT ===
Per claim: verdict, exact evidence, "what would falsify this", whether attempted, corrected wording if PARTIALLY PROVEN. End with a list of any claim that is technically true but where the CONSEQUENCE I stated does not follow — those are the most dangerous to post.

## C8 — Zephyr POST body omits `testCycleKey`

**PROVEN.**

`scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs:178-184`:
```js
async function postZephyrExecution({ testCaseKey, statusName, comment }) {
  return fetchJson(ZEPHYR_TESTEXECUTIONS_URL, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${ZEPHYR_API_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ projectKey: ZEPHYR_PROJECT_KEY, testCaseKey, statusName, comment }),
  });
}
```

Live capture of the actual serialized body from an executed run:
```
POST .../testexecutions
body: {"projectKey":"SFCC","testCaseKey":"SFCC-T285","statusName":"Fail","comment":"BrowserStack session: https://bs/s/1"}
```
Exactly four keys, in that order. No `testCycleKey`.

**Scope of the `testCycleKey` search:** `git grep -n -i "testCycleKey"` and `git grep -n -i "testcycle"` across the **entire tree** at `pr/61-live` (all paths, no filter) — **zero hits**. A broader `-i "cycle"` search over `scripts/`, `.github/`, `.env.sample`, `e2e/` returns only three unrelated hits ("cycle, never referenced again", "lifecycle scripts" ×2). The string does not exist anywhere in the repo.

**What would falsify this:** a `testCycleKey` set elsewhere (env-var injection, a wrapper, a spread into the body). Attempted — tree-wide grep plus a live capture of the serialized body. Both negative.

> ⚠️ **Whether Zephyr *requires* `testCycleKey` is a separate, external question.** I proved the code omits it. I did **not** prove the POST fails. `.docs/temp/SFCC-751-implementation-spec.md:204` itself lists this as unresolved: *"Zephyr's `POST /testexecutions` exact required-vs-optional fields beyond `projectKey`/..."*. Do not post "this will 400" as proven.

---

## C9 — Failed Zephyr POST → warning → continue → job still SUCCESS

**PROVEN.**

Exact path:
- `sync.mjs:319-324` — `try { execution = await postZephyrExecution(...) }`
- `sync.mjs:112` — `fetchJson` throws on non-2xx
- `sync.mjs:325-329` — `catch { warn(...); summaryLine('… **sync failed** …'); continue; }`
- `sync.mjs:62` — `warn = (msg) => console.error('::warning::…')`
- `sync.mjs:284,357` — `main()` falls out of the loop and returns normally
- `sync.mjs:359` — `main().catch(err => die(...))` — `.catch` never fires
- `sync.mjs:58-61` — `die()` (the only `process.exit`, line 60) is never reached

**Executed proof** (all three Zephyr POSTs returning HTTP 400):
```
::warning::… Zephyr execution POST failed for SFCC-T285: … -> 400 …   (×3)
| t-au | SFCC-T285 | Fail | **sync failed** | |                        (×3)
node exit code = 0
```

**Attack results — every counter checked, all negative:**
- Failure counter / `process.exitCode` / non-zero-on-all-failed: `grep -n -E "exitCode|process\.exit|failCount|failures|errorCount|\+\+"` over all 359 lines → only `process.exit(1)` at line 60 inside `die()`. None.
- Step-level check in `zephyr-results-sync.yml`: the sync step is `run: node scripts/zephyrBrowserstackSync.mjs` (`:117-118`) with no `grep`, no post-step, no `if: failure()`. The workflow's only `exit 1` is at `:100-101`, an unrelated artifact-availability guard.
- `::warning::` does not fail a step in GitHub Actions (only a non-zero exit does).
- **Not a required check:** `gh api .../branches/develop/protection` returns exactly three required contexts — `Storybook interaction & a11y tests`, `Unit tests (Vitest)`, `🔴 Branch Target Check`. "Zephyr Results Sync" is not among them (and structurally can't be — it's `workflow_run`-triggered).

**Precision note for the PR comment — don't say "silent".** The failure *is* visible: three `::warning::` annotations plus `**sync failed**` rows in the step summary. What's proven is that the job **conclusion is `success`** and nothing machine-reads either signal.

**Bonus finding (unclaimed, worth raising):** because the `continue` at `:328` skips the rest of the iteration, a failed Zephyr POST **also suppresses the Jira defect** for that failing test. My run showed 3 failing tests → **0 Jira Bug POSTs**. A Zephyr outage silently disables the defect-filing half of the pipeline too.

**What would falsify this:** any of the counters above existing. Attempted — all four, all absent.

---

## C10 — Wrong `getTestRuns()` shape → zero tests, exit 0, indistinguishable from empty

**PARTIALLY PROVEN.** The mechanism and the practically-relevant case hold; the claim's universal quantifier ("*not shaped as* hierarchy[].children[].details") does not.

**What is proven.** `sync.mjs:138-161`; `for (const suite of hierarchy || [])` at `:145`. Executed with a build **found** and `testRuns` returning the flat `{test_runs:[...]}` shape:
```
zephyr-browserstack-sync: ## Zephyr sync — build `Sprint-3-SFCC-751` (0 tests)
| Test | Zephyr key | Status | Zephyr execution | Defect |
|---|---|---|---|---|
exit code = 0
```
Control (build **not** found) prints a *different* line — `No BrowserStack build named '…' found — nothing to sync.` with no table — so the failure mode is distinguishable from "no build", and **indistinguishable from a legitimately-empty found build**, exactly as claimed.

**Where the claim overreaches — my attack partly succeeded.** Some malformed shapes *do* fail loudly:

| `hierarchy` value | Result |
|---|---|
| absent / `null` / `[]` / a string | silent 0 tests, exit 0 |
| `{}` or `{data:[…]}` (truthy non-iterable) | **THROWS** `(hierarchy \|\| []) is not iterable` → `main().catch` → `die()` → **exit 1** |

Also, a partial mismatch (`hierarchy[].children[]` present, `details` absent) yields `length > 0`, so the summary would *not* read "(0 tests)".

**Corrected wording:**
> If BrowserStack's `getTestRuns()` response returns 2xx but lacks a top-level array `hierarchy` — including the flat `test_runs`/`tests` shape the script's own doc comment says the first version wrongly assumed (`sync.mjs:36-46`) — the function yields zero tests, `main()` prints a `(0 tests)` summary, and exits 0, indistinguishable from a legitimately-empty build. (A truthy non-array `hierarchy` is the exception: `for…of` throws and the job fails loudly.)

**Attack results:** no shape assertion, no `die()` on a non-array, no empty-warning. `grep -n "testRuns\|\.length"` returns only the URL (`:142`), the interpolation `${testRuns.length}` (`:297`) and the `for` header (`:301`). There is no `if (testRuns.length === 0)` anywhere.

## C11 — `ZEPHYR_TESTEXECUTIONS_URL` derivation silently no-ops

**PROVEN.**

`sync.mjs:96`:
```js
const ZEPHYR_TESTEXECUTIONS_URL = ZEPHYR_API_URL.replace(/\/testcases\/?$/, '/testexecutions');
```

Regex tested with node:

| Input | Output |
|---|---|
| `…/v2/testcases` (**the `.env.sample:373` documented value**) | `…/v2/testexecutions` ✅ |
| `…/v2/testcases/` | `…/v2/testexecutions` ✅ |
| **`https://de.api.zephyrscale.smartbear.com/v2`** (ticket-prescribed base) | `…/v2` ⚠️ **NO-OP** |
| `…/v2/` | `…/v2/` ⚠️ NO-OP |
| `…/v2/testcases?maxResults=50` | unchanged ⚠️ NO-OP |
| `…/v2/TestCases` (case variant) | unchanged ⚠️ NO-OP |

**Executed consequence.** With `ZEPHYR_API_URL=https://de.api.zephyrscale.smartbear.com/v2`, the live capture shows the execution POST going to the **unmodified base**:
```
POST https://de.api.zephyrscale.smartbear.com/v2
body: {"projectKey":"SFCC","testCaseKey":"SFCC-T285",…}
```
and the summary column rendered `undefined` (`execution.key || execution.id`, `:332`) without the script noticing anything was wrong.

**Assertion on the derived URL: none.** The only validation is the non-empty check on the raw `ZEPHYR_API_URL` at `:76-78`. Nothing asserts the derived value differs from the input or ends in `/testexecutions`.

**Important context that cuts against reading this as a live bug:** the repo *does* consistently document the `/testcases` form — `.env.sample:373` and `SFCC-751-implementation-spec.md:154-157` ("*Note `ZEPHYR_API_URL`'s value is the full `/testcases` path … derive that from `ZEPHYR_API_URL` (strip `/testcases`)*"). **Half 1: PROVEN. Half 2: PARTIALLY PROVEN** (mechanism proven; consequence is external).

**Half 1 — invariance.** `computeBuildName.mjs:117-118`:
```js
const parts = [sprintNum, jiraKey, ...zephyrKeys].join('-');
console.log(summary ? `${parts} - ${summary}` : parts);
```
`grep -i -E "Date|now\(\)|random|run_number|RUN_ID|GITHUB_|uuid|timestamp|counter"` over the file → **zero matches**. No run number, no timestamp, no nonce. Output is a pure function of `(sprint field, jiraKey, @zephyr: tags in the checkout, issue summary)`.

*Precision:* "invariant across runs for the same Jira key" holds **provided** the Jira sprint field, the issue summary, and the set of `@zephyr:`-tagged specs matching that key don't change. Also **scope-limit it**: only `e2e-browserstack-preview.yml:172-178` (the develop-PR path) calls this script. `qa.yml:627-629` (release path) uses `github.run_number`, which *is* per-run unique. So the invariance only applies to develop-PR builds.

**Half 2 — `builds[0]`.** `sync.mjs:130-136`:
```js
url.searchParams.set('unique_build_names', BROWSERSTACK_BUILD_NAME);
const builds = body.builds || [];
return builds[0] || null;
```
No sort param, no ordering param, no `created_at` comparison. `grep -i -E "sort|order|latest|\.at\(|reduce|Math\.max|created"` over the whole script → **zero matches**. Confirmed by execution: given `{builds:[{id:'BUILD-OLD'},{id:'BUILD-NEW'}]}` the script used the **first** element.

Neither is observable without credentials — and per `sync.mjs:36-38` no build has ever existed under this account, so nobody has seen a real response.
>
> **Corrected wording:** *"`findBuild()` takes `builds[0]` with no explicit ordering and no `created_at` comparison. Combined with a build name that repeats across runs, correctness depends entirely on an undocumented BrowserStack ordering guarantee — worth pinning explicitly rather than relying on."*

Three verifiers in, V4 still running. The results are worth reporting now because **one of my claims would have embarrassed you publicly.**

## The catch that matters most

**C16 — my third-party list was wrong.** I claimed the access-gate header leaks to "Didomi, GTM, Contentful, Emarsys and every CDN." V3 checked:

- **Didomi: zero files** in the codebase (`grep -rli didomi` → 0). Not loaded at all.
- **GTM: zero files.**
- **Emarsys:** a doc reference, no loaded script.
- **SFCC Commerce API: not cross-origin** — proxied same-origin via `/mobify/proxy/api`.
- **Contentful: real.** `UiCopyProvider` is mounted in `_app-config`, so every page client-side fetches `cdn.contentful.com`.

The mechanism is airtight and the leak is real — but to *Contentful only*. As V3 put it, my version is falsifiable in about thirty seconds and would have discredited the whole finding.

## The headline claim now genuinely proven

**C2 — PROVEN empirically, mutation-tested.** V1 actually ran it rather than reading source:

| Invocation | Exit |
|---|---|
| real run, `--grep "@SFCC-NONEXISTENT-99999"` | **1** |
| real run, `--grep "@SFCC-999"` | **1** |
| **positive control** `--grep "@homepage"` | **0**, 4 tests |

It also confirmed `--list` doesn't short-circuit the check, `passWithNoTests` is set nowhere, the BrowserStack SDK doesn't inject it, and — by unpacking the obfuscated SDK — that Playwright's exit code actually propagates. That's the decoy discipline applied properly: the check was made to pass before its failure counted.

**But two corrections to how I framed it:**
1. **It does not block merge.** `Cross-browser E2E (BrowserStack)` is not a required check. It's red-CI noise plus a false Zephyr/defect signal — not a merge blocker. I said otherwise.
2. Blast radius is "every develop-targeted PR touching `overrides/**` with any ticket key whose Deploy Preview succeeded" — close to every real frontend PR, but not literally every PR.
3. **Unknown:** whether the red even appears on the PR's Checks tab, since `workflow_run` runs attribute to the default branch. V1 couldn't settle it. Flag as unknown, don't assert "a red X on your PR."

## Findings that got weaker

| Claim | What changed |
|---|---|
| **C9** "silent failure" | Not silent — it emits `::warning::` and `**sync failed**` rows. What's proven is the *job conclusion is success* and nothing machine-reads either signal. |
| **C10** shape mismatch | Overreached. A truthy non-array `hierarchy` **throws and exits 1**. Only absent/null/`[]`/string silently yields 0. |
| **C11** URL no-op | Latent, not live. The repo consistently documents the `/testcases` value that works. Frame as conditional on the stored secret. |
| **C17** `.env.sample` | `_EMAIL` isn't secret-class under the repo's own pre-commit guard, and `scope:tier` keys were *already* pushed as plaintext Variables. Real point is loss of per-tier isolation, not new exposure. |
| **C18** Edge | "Silently" **refuted** — the config documents the cut with a cost rationale. Edge *was* drivable (ran live at `73625dc`). Defensible finding is narrow: `architecture.md:23` is stale and this PR touched that line. |
| **C21/C23** | **Pre-existing**, not introduced here. Framing them as PR-61 defects is the fastest way to lose the room. |

## Findings that got stronger

- **C6** — PROVEN, and *this* one genuinely blocks merge. No `continue-on-error` anywhere in `qa.yml`, the GitHub API calls are bare top-level awaits, and `Unit tests (Vitest)` is confirmed required.
- **C20** — V3 pulled the actual 2.58 MB CI log. 60 test executions where 12 were expected, and the arithmetic reconciles exactly (5 platforms × 2 parallels = 10 workers). Real number is **~180 browser sessions** once `retries: 2` applies — worse than I said.
- **C14** — executed proof: 3 failing tests → 3 separate Jira Bug POSTs.
- **New, unclaimed:** a failed Zephyr POST also *suppresses the Jira defect* for that test — the `continue` skips it. A Zephyr outage silently disables the defect-filing half too.

## C15 adjudicated

Both prior reviewers were right, under different conditions. The discriminator is whether the failing test's title exists in `develop`'s tree — not pre/post-merge per se. Pre-merge: no assignee. Post-merge: silently wrong author. Three corrections to both: it's `git log --format=%ae` (**author**, not committer, and not `git blame` despite the function name), the wrong-assignee outcome depends on Jira user-search resolving, and that path is only reachable when the story is unassigned.

Waiting on V4 for the governance claims and the independent re-derivation of the `e2e_scope` counterfactual, then I'll give you the final post-safe list.

My script applied the *head* `e2e` file-group to both base and head. But this PR **added** `browserstack.yml` and `computeBuildName.mjs` to that group — at base only `qa.yml` was there. V4 says drop the HAR finding because "neither SFCC-751 document mentions HAR." **That's wrong — because I didn't give V4 the verbatim ticket you pasted.** It searched the repo's `.docs/temp/` specs instead. Your ticket says, in Deliverable 2:

> Attaches BrowserStack session URL **and HAR** to Zephyr execution record

So the requirement is real. But V4's substance is still valuable: the session URL **is** implemented, and the script documents that Zephyr Scale's REST API has no attachment endpoint, routing evidence to the Jira defect instead. So it's the same shape as Deliverable 1 — a sound technical reason, with the ticket never updated.

---

# Post-safe list

## Post these — proven, fairly framed

**1. `--grep` zero-match turns the BrowserStack Preview job red.** Empirically proven with a positive control; SDK exit-code propagation verified. Say: *not a merge blocker* (not a required check), affects develop PRs touching `overrides/**` with any ticket key, and `testing.md:371-373` documents the opposite behaviour. Flag as unknown whether the red surfaces on the PR's Checks tab.

**2. The coverage-comment step can fail a required check.** `qa.yml:285-368` — `if: always()`, no `continue-on-error` anywhere in the file, bare top-level `await`s on the GitHub API. `Unit tests (Vitest)` **is** required. **This one genuinely blocks merges.** Strongest small-fix finding.

Deliverable 3 unvalidated — and with `e2e-browserstack` now release-only gated, there's no reachable path pre-merge at all. **7. Hard Rule 7 inconsistency.** The author declined to pin `browserstack-node-sdk` citing Hard Rule 7 as out of scope, while adding `@vitest/coverage-v8` in the same PR without recorded integration-team approval. Cite his own spec line. Note it's a devDependency with no runtime impact.

**9. The access-gate header reaches Contentful.** `cdn.contentful.com` only, via `UiCopyProvider` on every page. **Do not name Didomi, GTM, Emarsys or SFCC** — zero of them apply.

**10. # Tier 2 — Protected Files

These can be modified on a feature branch but require a PR review from a developer who is not
the author before merging to develop.

> Paths reference `overrides/app/...` per this project's slim overrides layout. Override files
> keep the original Salesforce filename (kebab-case) but are TypeScript (`.ts`/`.tsx`).

## Global Shell (Owner: Both Squads — coordinate before touching)

```text
overrides/app/components/header/
overrides/app/components/footer/
overrides/app/components/drawer-menu/
overrides/app/components/list-menu/
overrides/app/components/seo/
overrides/app/components/_app/
overrides/app/components/_app-config/
overrides/app/components/uiCopyProvider/
overrides/app/routes.tsx
```

`uiCopyProvider/` is mounted once inside `_app-config` and provides `useUiCopy()`'s context
value to every page on every site — the same blast radius as `_app-config` itself, so it
belongs in this tier alongside it rather than defaulting to Tier 4 by omission.

## Shared Product Components (Owner: Squad B — notify Squad A)

```text
overrides/app/components/product-tile/
overrides/app/components/product-item/
overrides/app/components/display-price/
overrides/app/components/image-gallery/
overrides/app/components/swatch-group/
overrides/app/components/recommended-products/
```

## Shared Commerce Components (Owner: Squad A — notify Squad B)

```text
overrides/app/components/order-summary/
overrides/app/components/promo-code/
overrides/app/components/pickup-or-delivery/
```

## Theme Component Styles (Owner: UI Designer — notify before changing)

```text
overrides/app/theme/components/
overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts
```

One file per Chakra component (e.g. `header.ts`, `listMenu.ts`). Register new
files in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`. Foundations live alongside
in `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` and are **Tier 1** — see
[frozenFiles.md](./frozenFiles.md).

A component's own recipe may instead live beside it as `<name>.css.ts` (e.g.
`overrides/app/components/footer/footer.css.ts`) rather than here — see
[overrideStyling.md](./overrideStyling.md)'s co-location pattern, introduced with the
footer decomposition. It's still registered in `overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts`
either way. A co-located `<name>.css.ts` is **not** governed by this section's Tier 2
UI-designer gate — CODEOWNERS' `overrides/app/components/**/*.css.ts` rule routes it to
the owning squad(s) only. This folder's Tier 2 designation still applies to whatever
hasn't moved to co-location, and to genuinely cross-component shared values (e.g.
`footerShared.ts`) that a single component's file can't own.

`globalStyles.ts` is the `.zimm-*` global class registry, composed into
`theme/index.ts` as `styles.global`. It is derived from the `--zimm-*` variables in
`foundation/zimmTokens.ts` rather than defining brand values itself, so it sits at
Tier 2 — but it emits CSS on every page, so treat a change here as wider-reaching
than a single component override.

## Translations (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — notify before changing)

```text
translations/
overrides/app/static/translations/
```

## Shared Hooks — 5+ consumers (Owner: Both Squads — coordinate before touching)

```text
overrides/app/hooks/use-auth-modal.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-toast.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-modal-state.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-intersection-observer.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-currency.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-dnt-notification.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-app-origin.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-selected-store.ts
```

## Environment Switching Tooling (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — notify before changing)
`scripts/switchEnv.mjs` (`npm run env`) manages `.env.shared`/`.env.<tier>` locally and gates
`push` — writing shared/tier values to this repo's GitHub Environments (`shared` + one per
deployment tier under Settings > Environments) — to `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`. The
script's own gh-identity check is a fast-fail convenience only, same reasoning as
[AGENTS.md's Tier 1 Approval](../../AGENTS.md#tier-1-approval--how-its-actually-enforced) section
— the real enforcement is GitHub itself: writing an Environment Variable requires repo Admin,
which only tier-1-approvers hold. A careless change here could weaken that gate, or misroute a
personal credential (Jira/Confluence token, Contentful CMA token) into the centrally-shared
store instead of keeping it local-only — see the `scope:personal` handling documented in
`.env.sample`'s header before changing the scope-parsing logic.
```text
scripts/switchEnv.mjs
```

## Contentful Schema Definitions (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — notify before changing)

These files define the Zimmermann content model, authored once as a single
organization-scoped Contentful **Environment Template** (`npm run sync:contentful`,
via `client.environmentTemplate.*` in the `contentful-management` SDK) and installed
into each environment (`npm run install:contentful -- --target <env>`). This replaced
an earlier per-environment `sync.js` + migration-file pipeline once Contentful moved to
recommending organization-level content models over independently-synced
space/environment content types.

`content-types/*.js` is the sole source of truth per content type (including
`localized`/`required`/`validations` — there is no longer a separate migration file that
overrides an inferior default). Field deletion during an install is opt-in
(`--delete-deleted-fields`), off by default — a mistaken field definition pushed to the
production Contentful environment is difficult to undo and may break running components.

```text
scripts/contentful/buildTemplate.js
scripts/contentful/setup/installTemplate.mjs
scripts/contentful/content-types/
```

Always run `install:contentful` against a non-production Contentful environment first.
Requires `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` and `CONTENTFUL_ORGANIZATION_ID` (local / CI only —
never deployed to MRT).

# Testing Conventions

Three layers, three purposes. **Do not duplicate coverage across layers** — pick the cheapest layer that proves the behaviour.

**This is not license to skip a component's own test file because its behaviour happens to be
covered transitively elsewhere.** A component with real logic (branching, prop→JSX mapping
decisions, event wiring) gets its own `index.test.ts`/`index.test.tsx`, even when the state it
renders is owned by a hook that already has its own test, or a parent's assembly-level
Storybook `play` already exercises the rendered result. Resolve the duplication concern by
**scoping what that file asserts** — mock the hook/child component whose internals are proven
elsewhere, and test only this component's own contract (given a state, does it render the
right branch; given a DOM event, does it call the right handler) — not by leaving the
component with no test of its own. Relying on a *different* component's story to prove *this*
component's contract means the coverage isn't discoverable from the component's own folder,
and can silently vanish if that unrelated file changes. See
`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx` for the
resulting pattern (mocks `useSubscribeSection` and `ZimmSubscribeModal`, tests only its own
render-branch/event-wiring contract). A component with no branching or decision logic at all
(pure prop interpolation, e.g. `BottomBar`) still doesn't need its own suite — the exemption
below for single-parent internal components still applies there.

| Layer | Tool | What it covers | File pattern | CI gate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Unit | Vitest | Pure logic, data mapping, transforms, hook behaviour in isolation | `*.test.ts` co-located with the source | Every PR (`qa.yml`) |
| Component interaction | Storybook `play` | User-facing interactions in a single component (clicks, form fills, focus management) | `*.stories.tsx` `play` function | Every PR (`qa.yml`) |
| E2E | Playwright | Full user journeys across pages, multi-region, integration boundaries | `e2e/tests/**/*.spec.{ts,js}` | Every PR (`qa.yml`) — desktop + mobile Chromium against localhost/dev API; BrowserStack multi-browser on `release/**` only |

> Higher-level project rules: [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) > Testing. Day-to-day file conventions: [conventions.md](./conventions.md). This file describes **how** to write tests at each layer.

---

## What to test (and what to skip)

Write tests where failure would be **non-obvious** or **costly to debug**:

- ✅ Data mapping: Contentful → component props, locale/currency transforms, SFCC payload → view model
- ✅ Integration boundaries: Global-e pricing/tax logic, checkout ownership branching, consent gating
- ✅ Complex state: cart mutations, consent state changes, multi-step flows, optimistic-update rollback
- ✅ Pure logic that would survive a refactor invisibly if broken
- ❌ Re-exports, one-line passthroughs, type-only helpers
- ❌ Storybook visual snapshots — Chromatic/Loki belongs in a separate budget, not Vitest
- ❌ The framework — don't test that React renders, that Chakra applies styles, or that React Query caches

---

## Layer 1 — Vitest (unit)

### File layout

Co-located with the source, `.test.ts` suffix, never `.spec.ts`:

```
overrides/app/utils/formatPrice.ts
overrides/app/utils/formatPrice.test.ts
overrides/app/hooks/useCurrency.ts
overrides/app/hooks/useCurrency.test.ts
```

Components use `index.test.ts` next to `index.tsx` in the component folder
(see [components.md](./components.md) > Components).

### Structure

- `describe` blocks group related cases; `test` (or `it`) for individual cases.
- **Arrange → Act → Assert** pattern, one behaviour per test.
- Test names describe the behaviour, not the implementation: `"converts AUD to USD using the latest Global-e rate"` not `"calls convertCurrency"`.
- Use `beforeEach` for setup; clear mocks with `vi.clearAllMocks()` after each test.

### Mocking

- **Inline mock objects** for isolated unit tests — define plain JS objects right in the test file.
- **`vi.mock()`** for module-level stubs. Mock the smallest possible surface: a single function, not a whole module, when feasible.
- **MSW** is allowed for cross-functional integration tests (multiple modules wired together). Production paths must never depend on MSW — see AGENTS.md > Rules > "No mocking."
- Do not mock the thing under test; do not assert on internal implementation calls when an output assertion would do.
- **Known gap: `ZimmIcon` throws under Vitest.** It imports the base SFCC icons barrel
  (`app/components/icons`), which has a top-level side effect (`AmexSymbol.viewBox = ...`)
  that fails here because SVG imports resolve to raw path strings in this environment, not
  components. Not fixable from a test file — the SVG transform lives in `vitest.config.ts`,
  Tier 1 test config (AGENTS.md Hard Rule 8). Work around it by mocking `ZimmIcon` at the
  smallest surface in any test that renders an icon-consuming component:
  `vi.mock('app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmIcon', () => ({ ZimmIcon: () => null }))` — or,
  if an assertion depends on an accessible name the real `ZimmIcon` would carry (e.g. a
  fallback `<span aria-label>` with no wrapping interactive element), forward the relevant
  props instead of returning `null`. See `footerNavColumn/index.test.tsx` and
  `zimmSubscribeSection/index.test.tsx` for both variants.

### Commerce SDK hooks

Hooks that call `@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react` (e.g. `useCurrentBasket`, `useCurrentCustomer`) need a `QueryClientProvider` and `CommerceApiProvider` wrapper. Build a small `renderWithProviders` helper in `overrides/app/test-utils/` rather than duplicating wrapper boilerplate per test.

### What NOT to write at this layer

- Visual rendering — that's Storybook
- Cross-page navigation — that's Playwright
- Real network calls — never; use MSW or stubbed hooks

---

## Layer 2 — Storybook `play` (component interaction)

### When to use `play`

Every UI component has a `*.stories.tsx` (see [components.md](./components.md) > Storybook). Add a `play` function when there is **interactive behaviour worth asserting**:

- Form validation triggers on blur / submit
- Disclosure (accordion, drawer, modal) opens / closes via keyboard + mouse
- Focus moves correctly through a flow
- A controlled input's onChange wires through to the rendered output

If the story is purely visual (renders different prop combinations), no `play` is needed.

### Pattern

```tsx
import {expect, userEvent, within} from '@storybook/test'

export const SubmitDisabledUntilValid: Story = {
    play: async ({canvasElement}) => {
        const canvas = within(canvasElement)
        const submit = canvas.getByRole('button', {name: /submit/i})
        await expect(submit).toBeDisabled()
        await userEvent.type(canvas.getByLabelText(/email/i), 'name@example.com')
        await expect(submit).toBeEnabled()
    }
}
```

- Always query through `within(canvasElement)` — never reach into `document` directly.
- Use **`getByRole`** with an accessible name as the first-choice selector. Fall back to `getByLabelText` for form fields, `getByText` last.
- Don't import `userEvent` from `@testing-library/user-event` — use the Storybook re-export so the action is logged in the timeline.

### What NOT to write at this layer

- Multi-page flows — that's Playwright
- Heavy API mocking — keep stories visual, push integration assertions to Playwright

---

## Layer 3 — Playwright (E2E)

### Workflow

E2E tests follow the **three-stage gherkin-first workflow** (see [.claude/skills/qa-generate/](../skills/qa-generate/SKILL.md)):

1. Claude (or any developer) drafts a `.feature` file with Gherkin scenarios
2. Lead QA validates in plain English — **no Playwright code is written until sign-off**
3. Playwright spec is generated only after the `.feature` is approved

This prevents "technically correct tests of the wrong behaviour."

### File layout

```
e2e/features/         # Gherkin .feature files — source of truth, reviewed by Lead QA
e2e/fixtures/         # multi-region fixtures keyed by SITE_ID
e2e/support/
  helpers/            # shared helpers (auth, basket setup)
  pages/              # Page Object Model classes (BasePage, CheckoutPage, …)
e2e/tests/zimm/       # generated Playwright specs, mirroring features/
```

Spec filename convention for story-backed specs: `SFCC-NNN_short-description.<priority>.spec.ts`
(`.p0.` runs in the Digital SIT gate on `release/**`; on a `develop`-targeted PR, `e2e-localhost`
runs only the specs relevant to the diff — see **Change-scoped E2E** below). Jira-less smoke
tests use `SMOKE-{area}-{behaviour}.spec.js` instead — see
[e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md) > Smoke tests.

### Change-scoped E2E (`develop`-targeted PRs only)

`e2e-localhost` (`.github/workflows/qa.yml`) narrows which specs it runs based on the changed
files in the diff, instead of always running the full suite:

- Every spec must carry a Playwright test tag matching its Gherkin file's `@area` tag (see
  [e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md) for the tag list — `homepage`,
  `checkout`, `search`, `account`, `pdp`, `plp`, `integrations`) — and, per **BrowserStack story
  scoping** below, its `@SFCC-NNN` tag too: `test('...', {tag: ['@homepage', '@SFCC-142']}, async
  ({page}) => {...})`. Smoke tests (no Jira story — see
  [e2e/features/README.md](../../e2e/features/README.md) > Smoke tests) are exempt from the
  `@SFCC-NNN` half of this — `@area @smoke` only.
- `detect-changes`'s `Get changed files` step defines one file-path allow-list per area
  (`e2e_homepage`, and so on as new areas get specs). `Compute E2E scope` narrows the run to
  that area's `--grep` tag **only if every e2e-relevant changed file falls inside that one
  area's allow-list** — a single file outside it (a shared/global path, or one no area has
  claimed yet) falls back to the full suite, deliberately, rather than needing its own
  deny-list to maintain. `qa.yml`'s inline comments are the source of truth for the exact path
  lists — don't duplicate them here, they'll drift.
- `release/**`-targeted PRs always run the full suite regardless of diff — this narrowing only
  applies to `develop`-targeted PRs.
- **Adding a new area's first spec:** give it its own allow-list group in `qa.yml`'s
  `detect-changes` job, tag every `test()` in it with the matching `{tag: '@area'}`, and add it
  to this section. Forgetting either step doesn't lose coverage — an untagged/unmapped spec
  still runs under the full-suite fallback — it just misses out on the scoping optimisation.

### BrowserStack story scoping

`e2e-browserstack` (`.github/workflows/qa.yml`) is Zephyr-linked per-story execution, not a
general regression gate — that's what `e2e-localhost` and the Digital SIT gate are for.

- **`release/**`-targeted PRs:** always run the full `e2e/tests/zimm` suite, unscoped. A
  release aggregates a whole sprint's stories, so per-story scoping doesn't apply — Zephyr
  traceability still works, since every test carries its own `@SFCC-NNN` tag individually.
- **`develop`-targeted PRs:** `detect-changes`'s `Detect Jira story keys` step regexes
  `SFCC-\d+` out of the PR title, PR body, and branch name — the same signal the GitHub-for-
  Jira app uses to link a PR to an issue, so this needs no Jira API credentials of its own. If
  at least one key is found, `e2e-browserstack` runs `--grep`-scoped to that story's tag(s)
  (OR-joined if the PR references more than one). **No key found → the job doesn't run at
  all.** This is deliberate, not a gap: with nothing to attribute results to in Zephyr, there's
  nothing correct to run.
- If a key is found but no spec carries the matching `@SFCC-NNN` tag, `--grep` matches zero
  tests and Playwright reports "no tests found" without spinning up any BrowserStack sessions
  — a free no-op, not a failure, and not something that falls back to a full run.
- Every story-backed spec needs its Jira key as a tag alongside its `@area` tag (see
  **Change-scoped E2E** above) for this to work — the `qa-generate` skill adds both
  automatically. Jira-less smoke tests (`@area @smoke` only) never match a story key, so they
  correctly never run under BrowserStack — that's expected, not a gap; they're already covered
  by `e2e-localhost`.
- **Local pre-push equivalent:** `npm run test:story` (`scripts/runStoryTests.sh`) runs the
  same `browserstack-node-sdk playwright test e2e/tests/zimm --grep` command against real
  BrowserStack, so a developer can exercise their story before opening the PR. Pass the key
  explicitly (`npm run test:story -- SFCC-142`) or let it auto-detect from commit messages on
  the branch and the branch name — the same `SFCC-\d+` pattern, applied to local git state
  instead of PR title/body since no PR exists yet at that point. Requires `BROWSERSTACK_*` and
  the `E2E_*`/`PWA_E2E_*` vars in `.env` — see `.env.sample`. Manual, not enforced by a git
  hook — relies on developer discipline, not a blocking gate.

### Multi-region fixtures

Build SITE_ID-keyed fixtures from day one — Zimmermann has 8 storefronts across 6 regions (AU, US domestic, US international, UK, EU domestic, EU international, HK, ME) and 11 active locales. Do not retrofit. A test that hardcodes a region or currency cannot survive the rollout.

```ts
test.describe('Guest checkout', () => {
    for (const site of SITES) {
        test(`completes on ${site.id}`, async ({page}) => { ... })
    }
})
```

### Page Object Model

Selector priority — **enforce in code review**. Select elements the way real users (and assistive tech) perceive them:

1. **Accessible selectors** — role with accessible name, label, placeholder, visible text. `getByRole('button', {name: 'Add to bag'})`, `getByLabelText('Email')`, `getByPlaceholderText('Search')`, `getByText('Sale')`. First choice — these double as continuous a11y checks.
2. **Semantic selectors** — standard HTML attributes when no accessible selector applies. `getByAltText('Profile picture')`, `getByTitle('Close modal')`.
3. **Test IDs** — `data-testid` only when the element has no semantic meaning or text content (dynamic containers, canvas elements, loading spinners, complex layout blocks).

Never select by tag name, class name, or DOM position. The priority order keeps tests close to user experience and minimises `data-testid` clutter in the DOM, while still allowing a reliable fallback where semantics genuinely don't exist.

### What NOT to write at this layer

- Pure logic — that's Vitest
- Component interaction in isolation — that's Storybook `play`
- Network-mocked flows — Playwright always hits real SFCC APIs (dev org on feature PRs, SIT on the release gate). Do not stub network calls in Playwright tests.

---

## Test config files are Tier 1

`vitest.config.*`, `playwright.config.*`, `.storybook/`, `lighthouserc.js` are
**frozen** ([frozenFiles.md](./frozenFiles.md)). Do not modify them in a feature PR — config drift breaks every contributor's harness. Changes go through the Integration team.

---

## Quick checklist before opening a PR

- [ ] New component → has `*.stories.tsx`
- [ ] Non-obvious logic → has `*.test.ts`
- [ ] New user journey → has a `.feature` file (Playwright spec follows after Lead QA sign-off)
- [ ] `npm run test` passes locally
- [ ] No new MSW handlers in production-path code
- [ ] No edits to Tier 1 test config files

# Tier 1 — Frozen Files

These files must not be modified by Claude Code without the developer explicitly naming the file
in the prompt AND confirming they have spoken to the listed owner. No exceptions.

> **Note:** this is a slim overrides project on `@salesforce/retail-react-app` v10 — paths
> below reference `overrides/app/...` (the customisation surface) rather than the upstream
> monorepo `packages/template-retail-react-app/app/...` path.

## Design System (Owner: UI Designer — #design-system)

The whole `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` folder is Tier 1. Currently present:

```text
overrides/app/theme/index.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/index.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/colour.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/fonts.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/typography.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/gridSystem.ts

```

**Fonts are self-hosted and served on every tier.** `overrides/app/static/fonts/` holds two
Futura Round faces — Regular 400 and Medium 500 — declared by
`overrides/app/theme/fontFace.tsx` and mounted in both `_app-config/index.tsx` and
`.storybook/preview.tsx`. Only two faces exist because only two are used: all 22 textStyles
resolve to fontWeight 400 or 500, and `fonts.body === fonts.heading`.

There is **no environment gate** on this, and it is worth stating plainly because an earlier
revision of this section claimed there was. `ZimmFontFace` mounts unconditionally inside
`_app-config`'s `ChakraProvider`, and `pwa-kit-dev`'s `staticFolderCopyPlugin` copies
`overrides/app/static` in both the client and SSR webpack configs — so the `.woff2` are
published with every bundle and shoppers on every storefront render Futura Round.

`foundation/fonts.ts` already lists `'Futura Round'` first in both stacks, so the `@font-face`
declaration is the only thing that makes it resolve — no component, recipe or token changes.
The fallback stack renders roughly 13% wider, which is why serving the real faces matters for
design-parity review against Figma.

Per-component theme overrides live in `overrides/app/theme/components/` (**Tier 2**) or, per
the co-location pattern, beside their component as `<name>.css.ts` — governed by that
component's own CODEOWNERS entry instead, not this Tier — see
[protectedFiles.md](./protectedFiles.md). `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts`
is also **Tier 2** — it composes the `.zimm-*` global class registry from the `--zimm-*`
variables defined in `foundation/zimmTokens.ts`, so it is derived styling rather than a
brand token source, but it emits CSS on every page and therefore needs a named owner.

# CSS & Styling Conventions

Chakra UI and `.scss` conventions. See [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) > Rules > Styling for the
higher-level policy (Chakra props first, `.scss` only when insufficient, theme file
ownership/tiers) — this file covers the concrete day-to-day rules underneath that policy.

---

## Tokens — no hardcoded design values

Chakra UI props must use the Chakra token system — no hardcoded hex colours, no pixel
values for spacing, no raw font sizes. Tokens belong in
[overrides/app/theme/foundation/](../../overrides/app/theme/) (Tier 1 — see
[frozenFiles.md](./frozenFiles.md)).

```tsx
// ❌ hardcoded
<Box color="#1A1A1A" padding="16px" />

// ❌ a bare Chakra/theme token string — resolves correctly (theme.colors/theme.space ARE
// registered from the Zimmermann foundations) but is still not allowed in an override
// component; see overrideStyling.md's hierarchy point 2 for why
<Box color="text.default" padding="m" />

// ✅ token, as a raw var(--zimm-*) reference
<Box color="var(--zimm-color-text-default)" padding="var(--zimm-scale-m)" />
```

Type is its own case, not shown above — set it with `textStyle` (`textStyle="body2"`), never
a raw `fontSize`, per [overrideStyling.md](./overrideStyling.md) point 1. There's no
`var(--zimm-*)` substitute for the composite `textStyle` expansion itself, only for its
individual pieces (`var(--zimm-font-size-*)` etc.), so `textStyle` stays a bare key —
it's the one entry in the hierarchy that isn't a colour/spacing token.

**The raw-hex/px/rem/em half of this has a script but no CI gate yet.**
`npm run audit:tokens` (`scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs`) scans `overrides/app/components/**`
and `overrides/app/theme/components/**` for exactly this — see
[overrideStyling.md](./overrideStyling.md)'s `Never` note for the full scope and its
acknowledged-exception rules. It's not wired into CI (no `.coderabbit/ast-grep-rules/` rule
either), so nothing blocks a merge that skips running it — that's still a real gap, just not
an unstarted one.
The bare-token-vs-`var(--zimm-*)` half above **is** mechanically enforced for recipe files —
see `theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts`, which runs on every `npm run test` — though it
can't see the same mistake made as a JSX/`sx` prop; that half still relies on review.

---

## `.scss` — only when Chakra props are insufficient

Per AGENTS.md, reach for a `.scss` file alongside a component only when Chakra's prop system
genuinely can't express what's needed (e.g. complex pseudo-selectors, keyframe animations,
print styles). When you do:

- **File naming:** matches the component file exactly — `productTile.scss` next to
  `productTile/index.tsx` (see [conventions.md](./conventions.md) > File naming and folder
  structure for the folder layout this sits in).
- **Scoped, co-located only.** No global stylesheets outside `overrides/app/theme/` — a
  component's `.scss` file must only affect that component's own markup.
- **Nesting depth ≤ 3 levels.** Beyond that, the selector is almost always reaching into a
  child component's internals rather than styling its own root — a sign the styling belongs
  in that child instead, or that Chakra's `sx` prop / a theme variant would express it more
  directly.
- **No ID selectors.** Class-based only — an ID selector's specificity makes it
  disproportionately hard to override later (including by a legitimate future Chakra
  variant), and IDs aren't guaranteed unique when a component renders more than once on a
  page.
- **No `!important`** without an inline comment explaining why the override is genuinely
  unavoidable (e.g. fighting a third-party widget's inline styles) — same reasoning as the
  `any`/non-null-assertion escape hatches in [typescript.md](./typescript.md): allowed, but
  the reason has to be visible at the point of use, not left for the next reader to guess.
- **Prefer Chakra's `sx` prop or a theme variant extension over a new `.scss` file** for
  anything that's really just "a Chakra style the prop system doesn't have a named prop for"
  — a new global class is a bigger footprint than a one-off `sx` override, and `sx` keeps the
  style co-located with the JSX that uses it instead of a separate file to keep in sync.
